meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 16, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 and unanimously voted 7-0 to advance Concept B2—an 80-unit 100%-affordable LIHTC residential development paired with ground-floor retail, ~62,000 sq ft of office space, and a 260-space parking deck—as its preferred design for the Jackson-Pettigrew Street downtown site. Council approved 7-0 a Future Land Use Map amendment and Commercial General rezoning for 7130 NC Highway 751 (30,000 sq ft commercial, with self-storage prohibited via proffer and a follow-up 7-0 vote requested by Don Moffitt to ensure the zoning ordinance itself passed). On Item 27, Ample Storage's 200,000-sq-ft self-storage expansion at 4343 Garrett Road, Council divided 6-1—with Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Eddie Davis voting Aye and Don Moffitt voting No—on both the Comprehensive Plan amendment and the Commercial General rezoning, while voting 7-0 on the consistency statement after Moffitt switched his consistency vote to Yes. Council closed with 7-0 votes adopting initial Rural Residential zoning for 4618 Hobson Road following legislative donut-hole annexation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Recognitions, and Planning Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Council Member Eddie Davis led the Pledge with Troop 412, and Council recognized community events including a lead town hall at Holton Career and Resource Center and National Community Planning Month (accepted by Planning Director Patrick Young). City Manager Tom Bonfield also requested a closed session at meeting's end under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Dockless Bike Share Permits, Hybrid Bus Repowering, Duke Beltline Trail, Public Safety Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent headings covering Appearance Commission, street acceptances, Wake EMC service consent, dockless bike-share permit fees, Midwest Bus Corp. hybrid bus repowering, Duke Beltline Trail grant, Triangle Regional Model agreement, North Durham biosolids equipment, West Safety Services, auction authorization, August bid report, police/fire vehicle purchases, HUD fair housing and law enforcement grants, and City Code Sec. 70-95/70-96/70-129 revisions.

agenda_items.title: Jackson-Pettigrew Street Development Update (Concepts A1, A2, B1, and B2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson, DHIC's Michael Rogers, and Self-Help's Tucker Bartlett presented four development concepts for the two-acre city-owned site near the Durham Transit Station, comparing mixed-income versus 100%-affordable LIHTC scenarios with and without market-rate office space. Council members praised Mayor Bell's leadership in broadening the options, questioned parking ratios, pre-leasing risk, and affordable retail space for Black-owned businesses, and voted 7-0 to endorse Concept B2 (80 LIHTC affordable units with 25% at <=30% AMI, retail, ~62,000 sq ft office, and 260 parking spaces, carrying the lowest ~$2.8M post-voucher gap) as the preferred design.

agenda_items.title: FLUM Amendment and Zoning Map Change — 7130 NC Highway 751
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a 2.7-acre request across three parcels at 7130 NC 751 to shift from Office/OI(D) & RS-20 to Commercial/CG(D) capped at 30,000 sq ft with TIA roadway commitments (Planning Commission 12-0). At Council questioning, applicant agent Tim Sivers proffered a prohibition on self-storage; after voting 7-0 on the plan amendment and consistency statement, Council later voted 7-0 at `02:28:10` on Don Moffitt's motion to explicitly adopt the omitted zoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item — Ample Storage Sanding Creek (4343 Garrett Road, A1600014 / Z1600030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Ample Storage's request to re-designate 27–28 acres at 4343 Garrett Road from Medium-Density Residential/RR to Commercial/CG(D) for up to 200,000 sq ft of self-storage, preserving roughly 14 acres near a stream and proffering transit/light-rail right-of-way (Planning Commission 11-0). Council members debated self-storage concentration in southwest Durham, low job/tax generation, and Planning Director Pat Young's upcoming December white paper; Don Moffitt dissented 6-1 on both the FLUM amendment and zoning ordinance while switching to Yes on the 7-0 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning — 4618 Hobson Road (Session Law 2017-80 Technical Correction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented an exact-translation Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for 4618 Hobson Road, a donut-hole parcel inadvertently omitted from S.L. 2017-80 and annexed by July 31 technical corrections. With no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and initial zoning ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Endorse Concept B2 as Preferred Design for Jackson-Pettigrew Street Development (Item 25)
votes.discussion_detail: Following presentations by DHIC and Self-Help and council consensus backing the 80-unit 100%-affordable LIHTC housing, retail, and ~62,000 sq ft office option, Council voted 7-0 to direct staff forward with Concept B2.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Amending Future Land Use Map for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Tim Sivers' proffer excluding self-storage and Don Moffitt's remarks on commercial node creep, Council approved the comprehensive plan amendment resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map Amendment Resolution for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: After debate over self-storage concentration in southwest Durham, low permanent job/tax yield, and impervious surface versus voluntary stream buffering, Council approved the FLUM amendment 6-1 with Don Moffitt voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Initially tallied 6-1, Don Moffitt immediately asked the clerk to change his vote on the consistency statement to Yes, resulting in a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (CG(D)) for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the Commercial General with Development Plan rezoning for 200,000 sq ft of self-storage at 4343 Garrett Road 6-1, with Don Moffitt voting No.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Ordinance for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26 Corrective Vote)
votes.notes: Prompted staff commitment to refine motion sequencing in future planning agendas.
votes.discussion_detail: Don Moffitt raised a point of order noting the two earlier motions on Item 26 covered the FLUM amendment and consistency statement without voting on the zoning map change itself; staff concurred and Council approved the Item 26 zoning ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 4618 Hobson Road Initial Zoning (Item 28)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for 4618 Hobson Road 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance (RR) for 4618 Hobson Road (Item 28)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted Rural Residential initial zoning for 4618 Hobson Road 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Ample Storage Sanding Creek Rezoning and Self-Storage Concentration (4343 Garrett Road)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over amending the Future Land Use Map and rezoning 27–28 acres at 4343 Garrett Road to allow a 200,000-square-foot self-storage expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the FLUM amendment and CG(D) rezoning for Ample Storage's expansion.
side_a_arguments: Self-storage generates minimal additional vehicle trips on Garrett Road and provides affordable space for small startup trades and service businesses.

The development plan preserves roughly 14 acres (50% of the site) including stream buffers above ordinance minimums, offers potential transit right-of-way/bus stops, and follows Ample's high-quality brick aesthetic.
The Planning Commission recommended approval unanimously 11-0, and Planning Director Pat Young pledged a December white paper on future self-storage concentration rules.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose converting residentially designated land to Commercial General for additional self-storage.
side_b_arguments: Self-storage facilities generate extensive impervious surface, and roughly eight of the 14 undisturbed acres are already constrained by steep slopes and stream buffers rather than genuinely developable land.
Self-storage is proliferating across southwest Durham while providing very few permanent jobs, low tax yield, and no street-activating retail.
disagreements.resolution: Both the Future Land Use Map amendment and the CG(D) zoning ordinance passed 6-1 (Moffitt voting No), while the consistency statement passed 7-0 after Moffitt switched his consistency vote to Yes.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 2, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Steve Schewel excused 6-0 to attend his mother's funeral in Virginia, the remaining six Durham City Council members conducted a brief regular meeting featuring proclamations for National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, National Arts and Humanities Month, and Imagine a Day Without Water. Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda covering water reclamation facility improvements, youth workforce contracts, Fletcher's Chapel UMC sewer extension, brick paver repair, and DOST appointments. On its sole General Business item, Council voted 6-0 to adopt the revised City of Durham Social Media Policy for elected officials and appointed boards.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Steve Schewel, and October Proclamations

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 18, 2017 (1 of 2)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council encountered three split votes across a contentious September 18, 2017 meeting alongside unanimous 7-0 approvals of the consent agenda, the Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall rezoning, and a resolution supporting continuation of the federal DACA program. On Item 21 (Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Boards), Council voted 4-3—with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece voting No—to adopt an amended interim policy deleting board/commission content-based speech rules while directing staff to review First Amendment and public-records critiques for Thursday's work session. On Item 19 (Barbee Road Retail, 160,000 sq ft at Barbee Road and NC 54), Council voted 6-1 on both the consistency statement and rezoning with Charlie Reece dissenting over traffic capacity and commercial need. Finally, on supplemental Item 22 (117 Goodwin Road split-zoning cleanup to Rural Residential for Eno Animal Hospital), Council divided 5-2—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Bill Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden voting No—after nearby seniors raised fears over property taxes, traffic, and noise.

agenda_items.title: Youth/School Announcements, Rosh Hashanah Absence, Supplemental Item 22, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council praised Police Chief C.J. Davis and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden's school integration legacy, heard announcements on Read for the Record, and granted Steve Schewel an excused absence (7-0) for Thursday's work session on Rosh Hashanah. Council voted 7-0 to add supplemental Item 22 (117 Goodwin Road rezoning) and passed the consent agenda 7-0 (including FY16-17 budget carryovers, NC 54 corridor study, Triangle ITS plan, Vision Zero Durham resolution, and DPAC excess seating).

agenda_items.title: Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Appointed Boards/Commissions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece and Don Moffitt requested delaying the policy to address late-breaking public and First Amendment/public-records concerns raised by NC Open Government Coalition Director Jonathan Jones and others, while Jillian Johnson warned against adopting potentially unconstitutional content-based restrictions on board pages. Mayor Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden insisted on putting an interim policy in place immediately, leading to a 4-3 substitute motion by Moffitt (seconded by Cole-McFadden) adopting Reece's Sections 3/5 revisions and deleting board content-based restrictions pending Thursday's work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Moffitt, Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis Aye; Johnson, Schewel, Reece Nay)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Z1700002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a 0.5-acre rezoning along Renaissance Drive from CC(D) to CG(D) to incorporate the parcel into the existing 300,000-sq-ft Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall development plan without adding development (Planning Commission 10-0). With no public speakers, Council approved both the consistency statement and zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item — Barbee Road Retail (A1600011 / Z1600026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented Edens Land's request to change 14+ acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 from Office/RS-20 to Commercial/CG(D) for up to 160,000 sq ft of retail (Planning Commission 9-3). Proponent Jared Edens added floor proffers (at least 3 buildings, 15k–60k sq ft anchor, <=50% per building, no self-storage, internal sidewalks, west parcel cross-access, and conditional NC 54/Barbee left-turn signal), while opponent George Bryan warned NC 54 between Barbee and Revere Roads would exceed 110% capacity; Council passed both motions 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Zoning Map Change — 117 Goodwin Road (Eno Animal Hospital)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Brad Grinstead's request to unify a 1.5-acre split-zoned RS-20/RR parcel at 117 Goodwin Road under Rural Residential (RR)—a down-zoning that happens to permit an indoor-only veterinary clinic with no outdoor runs under 2 acres. Nearby residents Vera Hughes, Rev. Benny Torain, and Theresa Moody feared property tax spikes on seniors, noise, and traffic; Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Davis, and Moffitt voted 5-2 to approve, while Bell and Cole-McFadden voted No in deference to neighborhood seniors.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Continuation of the Federal DACA Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the resolution authored by Jillian Johnson supporting continuation of the federal Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program. Council unanimously adopted the resolution 7-0 before hearing public comment from Eliazar Posada (captured in Part 2 of the meeting video).

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence for Council Member Steve Schewel (Sept. 21 Work Session / Rosh Hashanah)
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Schewel requested an excused absence from Thursday's work session for Rosh Hashanah, which Council approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Add City Manager Priority Item (Supplemental Item 22: 117 Goodwin Road Zoning Map Change)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Bonfield requested adding supplemental Item 22 (inadvertently omitted from the work session agenda though properly advertised), and Council approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Amended Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Appointed Boards (Substitute Motion, Item 21)
votes.notes: Confirmed aloud on the record after electronic voting system misrecorded buttons.
votes.discussion_detail: Don Moffitt offered a substitute motion seconded by Cora Cole-McFadden to adopt the policy with Charlie Reece's edits to Sections 3 and 5, delete Subsection 3's content-based board restrictions flagged as First Amendment risks, and direct staff to review Jonathan Jones's email for Thursday's work session. After a voting-machine glitch, the Mayor and Clerk confirmed the 4-3 tally with Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis, and Moffitt voting Aye and Johnson, Schewel, and Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council closed the public hearing with no speakers and adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (CG(D)) for Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the zoning map change incorporating the 0.5-acre Renaissance Drive parcel into the existing auto mall development plan 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Barbee Road Retail (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: Following debate over NC 54 congestion, commercial need, and applicant proffers, Council approved the consistency statement 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Approve Barbee Road Retail Plan Amendment and Zoning Map Change with Floor Proffers (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the FLUM amendment and CG(D) rezoning including proffers prohibiting self-storage, requiring 3+ buildings (<=50% floor area per building, 15k-60k anchor), internal pedestrian connections, contingent west cross-access, and conditional NC 54/Barbee turn-phase signalization 6-1, with Charlie Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 117 Goodwin Road Zoning Map Change (Item 22)
votes.notes: Bell and Cole-McFadden confirmed as the two Nays (`02:36:31`-`02:38:03`).
votes.discussion_detail: Cora Cole-McFadden stated she would vote No out of deference to neighborhood seniors' fears, and Mayor Bell confirmed he also voted No. After correcting voting-machine display confusion, the consistency statement passed 5-2.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (RR) for 117 Goodwin Road (Item 22)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands correction confirmed Moffitt voted Aye and Bell/Cole-McFadden voted Nay.
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the Rural Residential rezoning for 117 Goodwin Road 5-2. When the electronic board misattributed a No vote to Don Moffitt, Moffitt confirmed by show of hands that he voted Yes, with Bill Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden casting the two No votes.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Supporting Continuation of Federal DACA Program (Item 23)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the DACA support resolution authored by Jillian Johnson 7-0, with Charlie Reece thanking Johnson and urging Congressional action.

disagreements.issue: Immediate Adoption vs. Delay of Elected Officials and Boards Social Media Policy (Item 21)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 over whether to immediately adopt an amended social media policy on the floor or refer it back to committee/work session to vet First Amendment and public-records objections raised by the NC Open Government Coalition.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt an interim social media policy immediately with floor amendments while scheduling work-session review of external legal critiques.
side_a_arguments: Council had already spent substantial committee time drafting guidelines and needed rules in place right away to prevent council members from posting personal views on official accounts.

Deleting Subsection 3's board content-based restrictions temporarily and incorporating Charlie Reece's Sections 3 and 5 edits mitigated immediate First Amendment concerns while leaving the policy open to Thursday amendments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay adoption and refer the policy back to the Procedures Committee or work session before voting.
side_b_arguments: Late addition to the prior work-session agenda deprived residents and open-government advocates of adequate notice and input.

NC Open Government Coalition Director Jonathan Jones raised serious First Amendment, public-records retention ('may' vs. 'shall'), and text-messaging gaps that require City Attorney vetting rather than rushed floor edits.
disagreements.resolution: Don Moffitt's substitute motion (seconded by Cora Cole-McFadden) passed 4-3, adopting the interim policy with floor edits and directing staff review for Thursday's work session.

disagreements.issue: Barbee Road Retail Comprehensive Plan Amendment and Rezoning (Item 19)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over rezoning 14+ acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 from Office/RS-20 to Commercial General for a 160,000-sq-ft shopping center.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the commercial rezoning with added design, anti-storage, cross-access, and transit/signal proffers.
side_a_arguments: Downtown/area-wide office land is already over-allocated by >100% for 30 years, and multi-family housing surrounding the intersection makes a walkable neighborhood grocery/retail node logical.

Floor proffers barring self-storage, capping anchor size at 60,000 sq ft across 3+ buildings, adding internal sidewalks and west cross-access, and improving Barbee/Grandale LOS mitigate design and traffic concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose commercial rezoning at the Barbee Road and NC 54 intersection.
side_b_arguments: The applicant failed to make a compelling case that another commercial center is needed near existing retail at Southpoint Mall, NC 55, and Fayetteville Road.
Nearby NC 54 segments (Barbee to Revere Road) already face severe congestion exceeding 110% of LOS D capacity.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and consolidated plan amendment/rezoning with proffers passed 6-1 with Charlie Reece dissenting.

disagreements.issue: 117 Goodwin Road Rezoning for Eno Animal Hospital (Item 22)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to unify 117 Goodwin Road under Rural Residential zoning to enable relocation of Eno Animal Hospital despite opposition from nearby elderly residents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve unifying the parcel under Rural Residential (RR) zoning.
side_a_arguments: Changing the split RS-20/RR parcel to RR is actually a residential down-zoning matching surrounding parcels rather than commercial rezoning, so it should not trigger commercial tax hikes.
UDO rules prohibit outdoor kennels on lots under two acres, and the clinic plans daytime hours and modern soundproofing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote No in deference to neighboring senior residents' concerns.
side_b_arguments: Nearby fixed-income seniors and church members fear increased traffic, noise, and property tax pressure in an established residential community.
Even if taxes may not legally rise from RR down-zoning, residents perceive real harm and deserve deference.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and the RR zoning ordinance passed 5-2 with Mayor Bell and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden voting No.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 5, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council unanimously approved 7-0 the consent agenda—including RDU FAA grants, corridor studies, the 2017 Downtown Parking Study, Fair Housing/Human Relations ordinance updates, and the Aquatic Facilities Master Plan—as well as consolidated annexations and exact-translation initial zonings for Pickett and Garrett (105 residential units) and 730 Delayer Drive (one residence). On Item 17 (Jacobs Glass, 4915 Hillsborough Road), Council divided 6-1—with Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Charlie Reece voting No—to require voluntary annexation alongside a water utility extension rather than invoking City Code Sec. 70-129(7)'s limited exception, before unanimously approving 7-0 the IL initial zoning. The final two hours centered on Item 18, Measurement Inc.'s statutory petition under G.S. 160A-538.1 to remove 21 downtown parcels from the Business Improvement District (BID); after hearing arguments from MI's counsel and strong opposition from DDI, downtown businesses, and Longfellow Real Estate, Council members uniformly opposed removing the parcels and adjourned 7-0 without adopting a removal ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Arusha Delegation, Proclamations (Hispanic Heritage, Recovery, Financial Literacy, Living Wage), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council welcomed a sister-city delegation from Arusha, Tanzania and issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Recovery Month, Financial Literacy, and Living Wage Month (noting Durham's path to $15/hour by FY 2018-19 and 97 certified living-wage employers). Charlie Reece promoted CenterFest and his Facebook Live agenda previews, Mayor Bell criticized inaccurate campaign claims about city spending, and City Manager Bonfield congratulated Howard University's football upset.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (FAA Grants, NC 54 & US 15-501 Studies, Downtown Parking Study, Fair Housing, Aquatics Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent headings covering Appearance Commission and Historic Preservation appointments, RDU FAA grants, Development Ventures HOME subordination, DCHC MPO corridor studies for NC 54 West and US 15-501, the 2017 Downtown Durham Parking Study, July bid report, R. Kelly Bryant Bridge Trail, Fair Housing and Human Relations Commission ordinance amendments, a National League of Cities financial inclusion grant, and the Aquatic Facilities Master Plan addendum.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Pickett and Garrett (BDG160010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Patrick Young presented Doc Nichols Partners' request for a utility extension agreement, annexation effective September 30, 2017, and exact-translation R-20 zoning for ~71.8 acres (6 parcels) allowing up to 105 residential units. Applicant Jared Edens highlighted non-mass-graded shoulder-and-ditch streets and 100-year storm detention reducing runoff into Garrett Farms by 60%, while neighbor John Robbins raised traffic and wildlife concerns.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — 730 Delayer Drive (BDG160017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Patrick Young presented Javad Kargar's request for a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation effective September 30, 2017, and exact-translation Rural Residential zoning for a 0.61-acre parcel to construct one single-family home. With no public speakers, Council approved both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Jacobs Glass (4915 Hillsborough Road, BDG170001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Patrick Young presented LR Jacobs LLC's request for utility extension, annexation, and Industrial Light (IL) initial zoning (PC 11-0) on 9.9 acres straddling Orange and Durham counties to build a 30,000-sq-ft warehouse. Engineer Chad Abbott asked Council to invoke City Code Sec. 70-129(7) to grant water service without annexation due to Orange County permitting confusion, but Manager Bonfield and Mayor Bell argued adjacent properties receiving city utilities must join the tax base; Charlie Reece dissented 6-1 on annexation before joining a 7-0 vote on initial zoning.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Measurement Inc. Request to Remove 21 Parcels from Downtown BID (G.S. 160A-538.1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andre Pettigrew introduced Measurement Inc.'s (MI) statutory petition to remove 21 downtown parcels from the Municipal Service District / BID. MI attorneys Bill Brian and Jeffrey Roether, Brian Sherrick, and Hank Sherrick argued MI provides its own 24/7 security, janitorial, maintenance, and marketing and that other corridors show greater crime/trash needs, while DDI leaders (Nicole Thompson, Lou Mair/Marish), downtown business owners, and Longfellow Real Estate testified that BID services and $5.25M city ID incentives directly lifted MI's property values; Council agreed MI failed the statutory test and adjourned 7-0 without taking removal action.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held; no removal action taken (adjourned 7-0)

votes.item_title: Approve Utility Extension Agreement and Voluntary Annexation for Pickett and Garrett (Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: Following testimony from Jared Edens and neighbor John Robbins and clarification from Steve Schewel and Mayor Bell on county-to-city density translation, Council approved the UEA and annexation 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement and Initial Zoning (R-20) for Pickett and Garrett (Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and R-20 initial zoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Utility Extension Agreement and Voluntary Annexation for 730 Delayer Drive (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming the lot supports a single house, Council passed the UEA and annexation by unanimous voice vote when the electronic voting screen failed to open.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement and Initial Zoning (RR) for 730 Delayer Drive (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and initial zoning for 730 Delayer Drive 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Utility Extension Agreement and Voluntary Annexation for Jacobs Glass (Item 17)
votes.notes: Supersedes preliminary annexation-only vote 25 seconds earlier at 01:17:32 (also 6-1, Reece No).
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 6-1 (with Charlie Reece voting No) on an initial annexation motion at `01:17:32`, then immediately amended and re-voted the combined motion including the utility extension agreement, passing 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement and Initial Zoning (IL) for Jacobs Glass (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and Industrial Light (IL) initial zoning 7-0, with Manager Bonfield directing Planning staff to coordinate with Orange County to avoid future review gaps.

disagreements.issue: Voluntary Annexation Requirement vs. Utility-Only Exception for Jacobs Glass (Item 17)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether to annex LR Jacobs LLC's 9.9-acre Hillsborough Road property along with its new water connection or invoke City Code Sec. 70-129(7) to extend utilities at double out-of-city rates without annexation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require voluntary annexation alongside the utility extension agreement.
side_a_arguments: The site is immediately contiguous to Durham city limits, posing no service-delivery obstacles that Sec. 70-129(7) was designed to address for remote sites along the I-85 corridor.
Entities seeking city water and sewer utilities—especially when receiving city services like fire and police—should join the municipal tax base.
disagreements.side_b_position: Invoke Sec. 70-129(7) to grant a utility-only exception at double rates without annexing the property.
side_b_arguments: The owner already completed an Orange County site-plan review in 2014–2016 without notice of Durham's annexation trigger and faces an extra six-month delay and lease extension costs.
Durham should avoid annexing property owners against their will when the city already collects double outside-city water/sewer rates.
disagreements.resolution: Council passed the amended utility extension agreement and voluntary annexation 6-1 (Reece voting No) and unanimously approved IL initial zoning 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Measurement Inc. Petition to Remove 21 Parcels from the Downtown Business Improvement District (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Following a two-hour public hearing under G.S. 160A-538.1(a)(1) pitting Measurement Inc. against Downtown Durham Inc. and downtown stakeholders, Council rejected MI's claim for removal and adjourned without taking action.
disagreements.side_a_position: Decline to remove MI's 21 parcels from the Downtown Business Improvement District.
side_a_arguments: Under G.S. 160A-538.1, Council retains discretion ('may' remove) and MI failed to meet the statutory burden because comparing downtown with BID services to non-BID neighborhoods ignores that the BID produces those clean-and-safe outcomes.
MI directly benefits from downtown's ecosystem, festivals, and $5.25M in city incentives for the Innovation District, and taxpayers cannot selectively opt out of district-wide investments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Statutory removal requested by petitioner Measurement Inc. (no seated council members supported removal).
side_b_arguments: MI's counsel and owners argued MI's 23 on-site security, janitorial, maintenance, and management staff plus private marketing render BID services redundant and other Durham neighborhoods show greater need.
disagreements.resolution: After City Attorney Patrick Baker advised no ordinance vote was required if Council declined removal, Council adjourned 7-0 with MI's parcels remaining in the BID.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 21, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting on Solar Eclipse Day with the electronic voting system offline (all votes taken by voice), the Durham City Council swore in the Durham Youth Commission, unanimously adopted 7-0 a joint City-County statement condemning hate violence in Charlottesville, and heard the 2017 Second Quarter Crime Report alongside extensive council discussion of local protests, police restraint, and false march-permit rumors. Council voted 7-0 on the consent agenda, referred six petitioned utility improvements back to staff for NCDOT talks, passed UDO Omnibus Changes 10, approved Fletcher's Mill (68 single-family homes), and adopted initial zonings for 421 Session Law 2017-80 donut-hole parcels across Wake and Durham counties. The meeting's lone contested vote came on Item 15, the Holloway Street Local Historic District overlay expansion (stemming from a 2010 petition): Council narrowly approved the modified expansion 4-3—with Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel, and Cora Cole-McFadden voting Aye to deter speculative teardowns of modest bungalows, and Bill Bell, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting No over split neighborhood survey support, fixed-income compliance burdens, and property-tax displacement risks.

agenda_items.title: Women's Equality Day, Durham Youth Commission Induction, and Joint Charlottesville Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum of Life and Science volunteer Reeves Sampson led the Pledge of Allegiance on Solar Eclipse Day, Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed Women's Equality Day, and Deputy Clerk Gray swore in new and returning members of the Durham Youth Commission. Charlie Reece introduced and Council unanimously adopted 7-0 a joint City-County statement condemning hate speech, hate crimes, and violence in Charlottesville, and Don Moffitt read a Human Relations Commission resolution.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items (Item 19 Reordering & Item 15 Protest Petition Invalidity) and Consent Agenda (Items 2-12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to move Item 19 to the top of public hearings and voted 7-0 to accept the City Clerk's ruling that a protest petition against Item 15 (Holloway Street Historic District) was invalid. Council then passed Consent Items 2–12 7-0, covering board reappointments, I-40/US 15-501 interchange, DCHC MPO transit planning, Neighborhood Bike Route, the Downtown Parking Garage GMP amendment, workforce/HIDTA/policing grants, and a Mobilitie telecom license.

agenda_items.title: 2017 Second Quarter Crime Report and Post-Charlottesville Protest/Rumor Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief C.J. Davis reported Part 1 index crime up 5% (violent crime up 6% though homicides fell 52%; burglaries at a multi-year low; Priority 1 response averaging 6.1 minutes), 28 sworn vacancies with a 63% surge in recruit applicants, 409 deployed body-worn cameras with auto-tagging, and a 50% drop in Part 2 drug violations alongside misdemeanor diversion growth. Council members commended DPD's restraint during local demonstrations (where one Confederate statue was toppled with no injuries) and debated social media rumors falsely claiming a KKK march permit had been issued.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing — Rescinding Six Previously Ordered Petition Utility Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reported encouraging initial meetings with NCDOT that could lower roadway compliance costs on six petitioned utility projects. After confirming affected residents had been notified and hearing no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and voted 7-0 to refer the item back to staff.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment — Omnibus Changes 10 (TC1700001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1700001 containing technical revisions and minor UDO policy clarifications previously reviewed by JCCPC, recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission, and approved August 14 by the County Commissioners. With no speakers, Council passed the consistency statement and text amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Holloway Street Local Historic District Overlay Expansion and Preservation Plan Update (X1000003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock reviewed a 2010 resident petition to expand the Holloway Street Local Historic District, previously tabled in 2013 after a 6-6 Planning Commission tie until 2016 consolidated review criteria were adopted. Proponents (Natalie Spring, Heath Beckett, Tiffany Graves, Susan Zhang, Rob Emerson, Jenny Tucker) urged preserving 1,000-sq-ft bungalows from teardowns, while opponents (Mark Galifinakis, James Bradford, Chris Dickey, Ram Neta) cited split neighborhood survey results, aged 2010 signatures (only 26% acreage / 28% lots), COA fees for seniors, and faster property-value inflation; Council unanimously passed technical updates and Area 4 removal 7-0 before approving the modified expansion 4-3.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Fletcher's Mill (2018 Fletcher's Mill Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Shamrock Capital Partners' request to rezone one parcel at 2018 Fletcher's Mill Road from Rural Residential to PDR 1.964 for up to 68 single-family homes (Planning Commission 13-0), noting a boundary buffer had been shifted outside a Duke Power easement. Applicant attorney Patrick Byker answered Council Member Steve Schewel's questions on student generation and brick ranch price points, and Council approved both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Session Law 2017-80 Wake County Initial Zoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented RS-10 initial zoning for 10 donut-hole parcels wholly or partially in Wake County annexed by the General Assembly under S.L. 2017-80 effective June 30, 2017, matching Raleigh's R-4 zoning (Planning Commission 10-0). With no speakers, Council approved both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Session Law 2017-80 Durham County Initial Zoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented exact-translation initial zoning for 411 Durham County donut-hole parcels annexed into city limits by S.L. 2017-80. Resident Barbara Gorman objected to her Hunters Ridge Trail property being annexed without direct city contiguity; Council expressed sympathy while explaining the state legislature mandated the annexation, and passed both motions 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Joint City-County Statement Condemning Hate Violence in Charlottesville
votes.notes: Electronic voting machine offline all meeting; all votes taken by voice/show of hands.
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece read and moved the joint City-County statement previously adopted by the Durham County Commissioners condemning hate speech, hate crimes, and violence in Charlottesville; Council passed it unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Reorder Item 19 to First Public Hearing (City Manager Priority Item)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's request to hear Item 19 first among public hearings.

votes.item_title: Accept City Clerk's Finding of Invalid Protest Petition on Item 15 (Holloway Street Historic District)
votes.discussion_detail: The City Clerk reported a protest petition filed against GBA Item 15 was ruled invalid, and Council approved the item unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Refer Six Petitioned Utility Improvements Back to Staff for NCDOT Discussions (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the City Manager's update on constructive NCDOT talks and no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and referred the six petitioned utility improvements back to staff 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for UDO Omnibus Changes 10 (TC1700001, Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Council closed the public hearing with no speakers and unanimously adopted the consistency statement for UDO text amendment TC1700001.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending UDO — Omnibus Changes 10 (TC1700001, Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO Omnibus Changes 10 text amendment ordinance by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Holloway Street Local Historic District Expansion (Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: Following extensive public testimony and council debate, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Remove Historic Designation at 208 N. Elizabeth St. (Area 4) and Adopt Preservation Plan Technical Updates (Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the baseline technical updates to the Holloway Street Preservation Plan and removed historic designation from 208 North Elizabeth Street (Area 4) by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Expand Holloway Street Local Historic District Overlay Excluding Area 1 and Including Areas 2 and 3 (Item 15)
votes.notes: Opposed members confirmed by show of hands at 02:19:25; Bell, Davis, and Moffitt each spoke explicitly in opposition prior to the vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Jillian Johnson moved to expand the Holloway Street Local Historic District as petitioned while excluding Area 1 (601 and 603 N. Queen St.) and including Areas 2 and 3. After debate pitting teardown preservation against neighborhood division, senior compliance burdens, and affordability, the motion passed 4-3 by voice vote and raised-hand check, with Bell, Davis, and Moffitt opposed.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Fletcher's Mill Zoning Map Change (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Patrick Byker's remarks on the 68-home Fletcher's Mill development, Council closed the hearing and adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (PDR 1.964) for Fletcher's Mill (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the PDR 1.964 zoning map change for 2018 Fletcher's Mill Road by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for S.L. 2017-80 Wake County Initial Zoning (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: With no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the 10 Wake County donut-hole parcels.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance (RS-10) for S.L. 2017-80 Wake County Parcels (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted RS-10 initial zoning for the 10 Wake County S.L. 2017-80 parcels by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for S.L. 2017-80 Durham County Initial Zoning (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: After hearing Hunters Ridge Trail resident Barbara Gorman's objections to state-mandated donut-hole annexation, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the 411 Durham County parcels.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance for S.L. 2017-80 Durham County Parcels (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted exact-translation initial zoning for the 411 Durham County parcels annexed by S.L. 2017-80.

disagreements.issue: Holloway Street Local Historic District Overlay Expansion (Item 15, X1000003)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 over expanding the Holloway Street Local Historic District overlay onto a seven-year-old 2010 resident petition amid deep neighborhood division over teardowns versus housing affordability and compliance burdens.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the modified Holloway Street Local Historic District overlay expansion (excluding Area 1 and including Areas 2 and 3).
side_a_arguments: Expanding the district provides a one-year demolition delay and thoughtful review to curb speculative teardowns replacing 1,000-sq-ft bungalows with $400,000+ houses.

The neighborhood contains significant early-20th-century historic residential structures meeting UDO criteria, and the seven-year delay since the 2010 petition was a city process failure rather than petitioners' fault.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose imposing the historic district overlay expansion on the petitioned neighborhood.
side_b_arguments: Even at its 2010 peak, petitioners secured signatures from only 26% of acreage and 28% of lots, and a current city survey showed roughly an even split (49-51) with half of original signers gone.

Imposing historic-district Certificate of Appropriateness procedures and fees burdens fixed-income seniors needing repairs or wheelchair ramps and risks accelerating property-value appreciation and gentrification displacement.
disagreements.resolution: Jillian Johnson's motion expanding the district (excluding Area 1 and including Areas 2 and 3) passed 4-3 by voice vote and show of hands.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 7, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council honored local activist Umar Muhammad and approved 3.5% salary adjustments for City Manager Tom Bonfield, City Attorney Patrick Baker, and City Clerk D. Ann Gray alongside the consent agenda (7-0). Two major policy items split the council 4-3: on Item 41 (property tax relief), Council Member Steve Schewel's substitute motion creating immediate property tax grants for Southside homeowners and studying citywide grants passed 4-3 (Ayes: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Don Moffitt; Nays: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis), and on Item 31, a cost-sharing plan capping homeowner paving assessments at $800 per lot while covering 100% of stormwater repairs (~84.9% city share) at Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates passed 4-3 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt; Nays: Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel). Council also unanimously passed updated Downtown and Ninth Street Design District UDO regulations (TC14-ZRS-03), three rezoning/annexation packages (4000 Danube Lane, Brightleaf at the Park paving-obligation release, Carillon Assisted Living, and Andrews Chapel townhomes), Sunday 10 a.m. alcohol sales, and a downtown sidewalk contract.

agenda_items.title: Poetry Fox Reading and Recognition of Activist Umar Muhammad
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece introduced local artist Chris Vitiello ('The Poetry Fox'), who read an original poem about Durham written in partnership with the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau and Duke Arts. Council Member Jillian Johnson then read a resolution honoring community organizer and criminal justice advocate Umar Muhammad following his fatal motorcycle accident.

agenda_items.title: Contract Amendments for City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered salary adjustments for City Manager Tom Bonfield, City Attorney Patrick Baker, and City Clerk D. Ann Gray effective July 1 following performance reviews. Members approved the amendments providing a 3.5% pay adjustment consistent with executive/employee merit benchmarks.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (including Item 15 Regional Transit Pass-Through Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Items 12, 31, and 33 for separate discussion and took up Item 15 briefly to clarify regional Durham-Orange County/Chapel Hill/Carrboro transit pass-through funding agreements. Remaining consent agenda items were approved in a single motion.

agenda_items.title: Property Tax Relief Program (Deferred Loan Proposal vs. Southside Grant Substitute)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield and Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented a deferred, zero-interest loan program with liens on resale/transfer for long-time low-income homeowners in Southside and Northeast Central Durham (NECD) hit by the 2016 tax revaluation. Council Member Steve Schewel objected to putting liens on senior homeowners and proposed immediate grants covering 2015-2016 tax increases for Southside plus a citywide grant study; Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Eddie Davis argued against sidelining NECD and adopting an unvetted grant program.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC14-ZRS-03: Design District Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock presented updates to Downtown and Ninth Street Design District regulations developed with focus groups and unanimously recommended (14-0) by the Planning Commission. Council Member Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece questioned a proposed exemption near Rigsby Street before adopting the amendment incorporating Rigsby Street cleanup revisions.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning: 4000 Danube Lane (81 Single-Family Lots)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and zoning map change from Woodstone Homes for 81 single-family lots at 4000 Danube Lane, where developer attorney Patrick Byker proffered $15,000 for Durham Public Schools. Council approved the annexation, utility agreement, and zoning map change.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change & Plan Amendment: Brightleaf at the Park (PDR 3.99 to PDR 1.902)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker represented El Star Management in requesting a downzoning and removal of an obligation to pave roughly 900 feet of the unfunded Northern Durham Parkway while keeping all 120-foot right-of-way dedicated. Resident Sean Jekyll urged escrow payment instead and disputed an HOA Watch letter submitted to the Planning Commission, while Council Member Don Moffitt endorsed removing the 'road to nowhere' paving mandate alongside reduced density.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Carillon Assisted Living of North Durham (412 & 4214 Guess Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak and applicant representative Robert Stenson presented a 14.34-acre rezoning to PDR 3.906 for a 56-room, up to 84-bed assisted living and memory care facility accepting Medicaid/state assistance in North Durham. Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and zoning map change.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Andrews Chapel Townhome Allocation Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and engineer Chris Mayle presented an amendment to the 114.17-acre Andrews Chapel PDR 4.793 development enlarging the townhome envelope and shifting proportions toward townhomes within the 500-unit cap. Council Member Charlie Reece thanked the developer for outparcel concessions along Andrews Chapel Road before unanimous approval.

agenda_items.title: City Code Amendment: Sunday Morning Alcohol Sales Starting at 10:00 AM
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following state legislation authorizing local 'brunch bill' ordinances, City Attorney Patrick Baker clarified that the amendment allows ABC-permitted restaurants and retail establishments to sell alcohol at 10:00 a.m. instead of noon on Sundays. Speaker Minister Zia opposed the change on moral and public-safety grounds, while Mayor Bell cited local pastoral input supporting passage.

agenda_items.title: Ravenstone & Stonehill Estates Failed Subdivisions: Stormwater & Paving Assessments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams and Deputy Director Robert Joyner outlined options to finish failing developer-abandoned streets and stormwater ponds in Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates after bond litigation recovery (~$440,000 shortfall after $210,000 legal recovery on ~$1M+ total work). Residents pleaded for relief after paying steep assessments or facing flood risk, while Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, and Charlie Reece opposed covering 100% of HOA stormwater obligations ahead of low-income/older neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Sidewalk Repair Contract & Excused Work Session Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel questioned Assistant Public Works Director Tasha Johnson on prioritizing sidewalks around the north and east sides of City Hall ahead of Church Street and other neighborhoods; staff explained service backlogs and two-way loop compatibility. Council unanimously approved the contract and an excused work session absence before adjourning at 10:35 p.m.

votes.item_title: Resolution Honoring Community Organizer Umar Muhammad
votes.notes: Read by Council Member Jillian Johnson; unanimously adopted.
votes.discussion_detail: Resolution honoring Durham organizer Umar Muhammad (Southern Coalition for Social Justice / Forward Justice).

votes.item_title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Contract Amendments (3.5% Pay Adjustment)
votes.notes: Approved 7-0 effective July 1.
votes.discussion_detail: Charter officer compensation adjustments matching merit benchmarks.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 12, 31, and 33)
votes.notes: Items 12, 31, and 33 pulled for separate consideration; Item 15 transit agreements clarified prior to vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved remaining consent items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 41: Property Tax Relief Grant Program (Substitute Motion for Southside Grants & Citywide Study)
votes.notes: Mayor Bell explicitly read the three 'No' votes aloud: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eddie Davis.
votes.discussion_detail: Main motion to adopt staff's deferred loan program with liens on NECD/Southside homes was superseded by substitute motion adopting Steve Schewel's grant approach.

votes.item_title: Item 43: UDO Text Amendment TC14-ZRS-03 (Design District Revisions)
votes.notes: Vote passed unanimously on updated Downtown and Ninth Street Design District UDO rules.
votes.discussion_detail: Form-based district technical and design refinements.

votes.notes: Woodstone Homes 81-lot single-family project with voluntary $15,000 DPS proffer; annexation, utility extension, consistency statement, FLUM change, and zoning map change approved via sequential unanimous votes concluding at 01:42:07.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves 4000 Danube Lane annexation, utility extension, FLUM amendment, and residential rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 45: Brightleaf at the Park Plan Amendment, Consistency Statement & Rezoning (PDR 1.902)
votes.notes: Three sequential unanimous 7-0 votes (plan amendment, consistency statement, zoning map change) finishing at 02:04:30.
votes.discussion_detail: Downzones Brightleaf from PDR 3.99 to PDR 1.902 and releases developer from paving ~900 feet of Northern Durham Parkway while keeping 120-ft ROW dedicated.

votes.item_title: Item 46: Carillon Assisted Living of North Durham (Consistency & Rezoning PDR 3.906)
votes.notes: Sequential consistency statement and rezoning votes passed unanimously without objection.
votes.discussion_detail: 56-room (up to 84-bed) assisted living and Alzheimer's facility at 412 & 4214 Guess Road.

votes.item_title: Item 47: Andrews Chapel Zoning Map Change (Consistency Statement & Ordinance)
votes.notes: Consistency statement passed 7-0 at 02:13:34 and rezoning ordinance passed 7-0 at 02:13:52.
votes.discussion_detail: Enlarged townhome building/parking envelope and proportion within 500-unit PDR 4.793 project.

votes.item_title: Item 12: City Code Amendment Allowing Sunday Morning Alcohol Sales at 10:00 AM
votes.notes: Passed 7-0 following public opposition from Minister Zia.
votes.discussion_detail: Implements NC local option shifting Sunday alcohol sales start from 12:00 p.m. to 10:00 a.m.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Ravenstone & Stonehill Estates Infrastructure Completion & Assessment Cap
votes.notes: Caps homeowner paving assessment at $800/lot (~10% of paving cost) while city funds remaining paving and 100% of stormwater work (~84.9% total city share). Nays explicitly named: Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel.
votes.discussion_detail: Split vote over relieving failed-subdivision homeowners vs. subsidizing HOA stormwater maintenance.

votes.item_title: Item 33: Downtown Sidewalk Repair Contract & Excused Work Session Absence
votes.notes: Sidewalk repair contract passed 7-0 at 03:36:45; excused absence approved 7-0 at 03:37:04.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved sidewalk repairs around City Hall and downtown corridors.

disagreements.issue: Property Tax Relief Delivery Model: Deferred Liens vs. Direct Grants (Item 41)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 over whether to assist long-time low-income homeowners facing steep 2016 post-revaluation tax increases through staff's proposed deferred loan program with property liens (covering both Southside and Northeast Central Durham) or via direct, non-repayable grants beginning immediately in Southside while studying citywide expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support immediate direct grants covering 2015-2016 tax increases for Southside homeowners and commission a citywide grant study rather than imposing deferred-loan liens on seniors.
side_a_arguments: Deferred loans place liens on elderly homeowners' homes and discourage participation, whereas modest direct grants keep residents stably housed.
Southside gentrification and city investment triggered sharp assessments that immediate grants can offset while staff designs a broader framework.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt the vetted staff deferred-loan program immediately for both Southside and Northeast Central Durham rather than narrowing initial aid or risking unvetted grant legality.
side_b_arguments: Staff worked 10 months to produce a fiscally and legally vetted program covering both NECD and Southside.
Switching to grants without county buy-in leaves NECD residents in limbo and lacks confirmed legal/fiscal vetting.
disagreements.resolution: Substitute grant motion passed 4-3 at 01:12:11.

disagreements.issue: City Cost-Share for Failed Subdivisions: Ravenstone & Stonehill Estates (Item 31)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 over capping lot assessments at $800 for street paving and funding 100% of stormwater repairs (~84.9% overall city share) in the developer-abandoned Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates subdivisions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Cap paving assessments at $800 per lot and cover 100% of stormwater infrastructure remediation because city bond-collection failures left buyers exposed.
side_a_arguments: Residents bought homes relying on city subdivision plat approvals and developer performance bonds that the city failed to call on time.
Middle- and working-class homeowners had already paid substantial HOA/remediation expenses and cannot afford steep special assessments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose absorbing 100% of HOA stormwater maintenance/repair costs and deep general-fund subsidies beyond standard petition ratios.
side_b_arguments: Using taxpayer funds to pay 100% of private HOA stormwater detention ponds sets an unsustainable precedent not extended to lower-income older neighborhoods lacking infrastructure.
Citywide equity demands spending public stormwater and paving dollars where residents have the greatest need rather than subsidizing newer HOA subdivisions.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-3 at 03:33:40.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 19, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council unanimously adopted the FY 2017-2018 budget and FY 2018-2023 Capital Improvement Plan (Item 7, 7-0)—doubling the dedicated affordable housing fund to $5.5 million, raising minimum city pay to $15/hour, adding 12 weeks paid parental leave, and funding 35 firefighters for Station 17—along with the consent agenda (7-0) and the FY 2017-2018 HUD Annual Action Plan (7-0). Council approved Village Hearth Cohousing's annexation and rezoning (7-0), but unanimously rejected 0-7 the 90-home voluntary annexation at 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard (Item 28) via an affirmative motion moved by Don Moffitt with intent to vote against (Ayes: none; Nays: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt) due to traffic funneling down narrow Marchery Road and jurisdictional donut-hole concerns. Finally, council held open until August 21 the public hearing on rescinding six stalled 2007-era utility extension petitions (Item 30) after sharp debate over absorbing $2.15 million in NCDOT shoring and road reconstruction cost increases.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight Awards & Americans for the Arts Prosperity 5 Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented Neighborhood Spotlight Awards for May and June 2017 to East Durham volunteer George A. Long Sr. and Waterbury/Lansbury park advocate John Goebel. Council also proclaimed support for the Arts & Economic Prosperity 5 study presented by Durham Arts Council CEO Sherry DeVries, noting $154.1 million in annual nonprofit arts economic activity in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Adoption of FY 2017-2018 Budget & Capital Improvement Plan (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda unanimously after Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden pressed staff on workforce diversity for vendor Item 17. On Item 7 (the FY 2017-2018 Budget), speaker Chris Tiffany criticized police spending; Council Members Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Don Moffitt, and Mayor Bell praised doubling the housing fund to $5.5M, adopting $15/hr minimum pay, 12 weeks parental leave, $6.5M street paving, 35 firefighters, and closing Fayette Place.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning: 1000 Infinity Road (Village Hearth Cohousing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins and cohousing representatives Pat Garren and architect Chuck Flink presented a 15-acre voluntary annexation, utility agreement, and PDR 1.870 rezoning for a 28-unit 55+ LGBT-focused senior cohousing community in the Eno River watershed with 75% open space. Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0; Council approved annexation, utility agreement, consistency statement, and rezoning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning: 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard (Hire Properties 90 Homes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a 24.4-acre voluntary annexation and RS-8 straight zoning request for ~90 single-family homes that would create jurisdictional donut holes and route traffic through narrow Marchery Road rather than upgrading unpaved Atkins Heights Boulevard to Fayetteville Road. Nearby residents opposed Marchery Road traffic (~900 trips/day); Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval with the stated intent to vote against, leading to a unanimous rejection.

agenda_items.title: Third Public Hearing & Approval of Draft FY 2017-2018 Annual Action Plan (HUD Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Coordinator Wilma Conyers presented final HUD entitlement allocations ($1.798M CDBG, $822K HOME, $165K ESG, $335K HOPWA) for the FY 2017-2018 Annual Action Plan ahead of the August 16 HUD deadline. With no public speakers signed up, Don Moffitt moved approval including accompanying grant ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Resolution to Rescind Six Petitioned Utility Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams and NC Utilities Commission Public Staff representative Mr. Ferrazzet reviewed escalated costs ($2.15M+) driven by NCDOT active-shoring and road-reconstruction mandates on six 2007 utility extension petitions outside city limits, including Grand Oaks/Red Coach's failing package sewer plant. After Ravenstone HOA Vice President Jonathan McLean opposed subsidizing non-city residents while homeowners pleaded over failing septic/wells, Council kept the hearing open until August 21 to seek NCDOT cost relief and annexation revenue estimates.

disagreements.issue: Road Connectivity & Donut Holes: 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard Annexation (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: While council members ultimately voted 0-7 to reject the 90-home voluntary annexation, members debated whether straight-zoned residential connectivity via Marchery Road should be rejected outright without a dedicated Fayetteville Road outlet on Atkins Heights Boulevard.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reject funneling 90 single-family homes onto narrow Marchery Road without improving Atkins Heights Boulevard out to Fayetteville Road and avoid creating large unincorporated donut holes.
side_a_arguments: Adding ~900 daily trips solely down Marchery Road without a Fayetteville Road connection threatens emergency vehicle access and burdens an existing 43-home subdivision.
Voluntary annexation creates large unincorporated service donut holes while straight zoning offers no enforceable off-site improvements.
disagreements.side_b_position: Explore whether staff traffic standards considered Marchery Road adequate before concluding straight zoning could not protect neighbors.
side_b_arguments: Ordinance connectivity rules normally favor linking 50-foot public subdivision streets, though straight zoning prevents council from binding the developer to improve Atkins Heights.
disagreements.resolution: Rejected unanimously 0-7 at 02:03:09 after Don Moffitt moved approval with intent to vote against.

disagreements.issue: Paying $2.15M+ Cost Escalations vs. Rescinding Six County Utility Petitions (Item 30)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to absorb $2.152 million in NCDOT active-shoring and road reconstruction cost escalations for outside-city county utility petitions ordered in 2007 (including Grand Oaks/Red Coach's failing package plant) or pursue rescission/annexation and NCDOT cost-sharing.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold the city to its 2007 commitment and absorb the cost increase on behalf of affected homeowners with failing wells and septic systems.
side_a_arguments: Homeowners relied for ten years on city utility orders in making housing decisions; moral fairness requires the city to bear increases caused by NCDOT changes and project delays.
disagreements.side_b_position: Seek NCDOT cost-sharing or waiver relief and study city-tax revenue from potential annexation before committing city taxpayers to pay $2.15M for county parcels.
side_b_arguments: Using city taxpayer funds for non-city residents whose properties do not pay city taxes raises major fiscal equity objections (echoed by Ravenstone HOA).
State transportation mandates caused most of the cost spike, so city and NC Utilities Commission staff should press NCDOT for relief first.
disagreements.resolution: Public hearing held open until August 21 pending August 10 work-session review of NCDOT talks and annexation estimates.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 5, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: In a marathon six-hour session ending near 1:00 a.m., the Durham City Council passed three deeply contested land-use decisions alongside routine business and the consent agenda (7-0). On Item 28 (Watkins at Weatherspoon, 300 mixed-use units near Patterson Place), the consistency statement passed 6-1 (Nays: Charlie Reece) and the rezoning passed 4-3 by show of hands (voting machine offline; Eddie Davis, Steve Schewel, and Cora Cole-McFadden spoke in support, Jillian Johnson spoke in opposition, Charlie Reece and Don Moffitt expressed design/affordability concerns, and the clerk did not read the seven hand votes aloud). On Item 29 (1201 Ellis Road, 180 Dan Ryan Builders townhomes), both the comprehensive plan amendment and the rezoning passed 4-3 by show of hands without individual names read aloud into the record, while the consistency statement passed unanimously (7-0). Finally, on Item 27 (North River Village / Publix at Guess and Latta Roads), Council rejected both the consistency statement and the rezoning 1-6 (Ayes: Eddie Davis; Nays: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Don Moffitt) on grounds that a suburban shopping center conflicted with low-density comprehensive planning, lacked transit access, and undermined existing North Durham commercial centers.

agenda_items.title: Retiree Resolution, Consent Agenda, and Item 17/23 Affordable Housing & Job Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved routine resolutions, the consent agenda (7-0), and several pulled economic/housing items including Item 17 (Neighborhood Improvement Services community job development), Item 20, and Item 23 (Jackson/Pettigrew Street affordable housing site). On Item 23, Charlie Reece criticized distributing a last-minute funding increase at the dais without public notice, while Don Moffitt moved increasing design funding from $125,500 to $199,500 to pursue 80 LIHTC affordable units; all passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017-2018 Budget & FY 2017-2018 Annual Action Plan Second Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff conducted formal public hearings on the proposed FY 2017-2018 budget and federal CDBG/HOME Annual Action Plan prior to final adoption later in June. Residents and advocates testified on funding priorities including housing stability and neighborhood services.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Watkins at Weatherspoon (3312 Watkins Road, 300 Units + Commercial)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The developer requested Mixed-Use zoning near the future Patterson Place light-rail station, proffering $150,000 toward the Affordable Housing Fund and $15,000 for DPS while modeling Downtown/Ninth Street Design District principles. Jillian Johnson argued the project locked in only 1% equivalent affordability ahead of the Patterson Place Compact Neighborhood Design District, Don Moffitt echoed timing worries, and Eddie Davis, Steve Schewel, and Cora Cole-McFadden backed proactive density near transit; consistency passed 6-1 and rezoning passed 4-3.

agenda_items.title: Plan Amendment & Rezoning: 1201 Ellis Road (Dan Ryan Builders 180 Townhomes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jared Eaton represented Dan Ryan Builders on a 23-acre rezoning from RR to PDR 7.870 for up to 180 townhomes with a 61-foot future River Road ROW reservation and proffers of $25,000 for affordable housing and $5,500 for DPS. Neighbors Betty Mangum and Thomas Lines opposed over Theodore Lane branch safety, debris, stormwater runoff, and Riddle/Ellis traffic, while Planning Commission had backed the case 8-3; both the plan amendment and rezoning passed 4-3.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Plan Amendment & Rezoning Passed 4-3; Consistency Passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Lumley Road Townhomes Annexation/Rezoning & UDO Text Amendment TC17-03 (A-65 Airport Overlay)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Darlington Advisors sought voluntary annexation and RS-M zoning (up to 108 townhomes) at 576 Lumley Road with a voluntary $10,000 DPS pledge, passing unanimously across five sequential motions. Council also unanimously approved UDO text amendment TC17-03 allowing utilities (subject to special use permit) in two parcels within RDU's A-65 airport noise overlay.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: North River Village (Publix Mixed-Use at Guess & Latta Roads)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Postponed to the end of public hearings due to massive turnout, the 29.8-acre mixed-use request anchored by a Publix grocery drew hours of testimony over traffic, runoff, suburban sprawl vs. North Durham retail investment, and grocery jobs. Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, and Cora Cole-McFadden opposed on comprehensive-plan, horizontal mixed-use integrity, greenfield vs. infill, and transit grounds, while Eddie Davis argued in favor; both consistency and rezoning failed 1-6.

agenda_items.title: Open Space & Trails and Human Relations Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Open Space & Trails Commission appointments passed unanimously, ballot results for the Human Relations Commission left two remaining vacancies short of majority support until Don Moffitt switched his vote and Jillian Johnson withdrew her holdover request. Council then unanimously appointed Nathan Plummer and John Rooks before adjourning.

votes.notes: Open Space & Trails passed unanimously at 05:48:20/05:49:44; Human Relations Commission appointments (Nathan Plummer at 05:53:13, John Rooks at 05:54:21) passed unanimously after Don Moffitt switched his vote and Jillian Johnson withdrew holdover.

disagreements.issue: Affordable Housing Targets & Design District Timing: Watkins at Weatherspoon (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: Council passed the 300-unit Watkins at Weatherspoon mixed-use rezoning 4-3 (after 6-1 consistency approval) amid sharp debate over whether to approve early transit-oriented density with a $150,000 cash proffer or wait ~9-12 months for the Patterson Place Compact Neighborhood Design District to incentivize Durham's 15% affordable housing goal.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the project now as a vertically integrated mixed-use investment supporting light rail, school/housing proffers, and tax base growth.
side_a_arguments: Developers voluntarily modeled Downtown/Ninth Street Design District guidelines and proffered $150,000 for affordable housing, $15,000 for DPS, and transit assistance without legal compulsion.
With scarce housing bond/tax dollars prioritized for DHA, Jackson Street, DCLT, and CASA, Patterson Place would likely see little city subsidy even after the overlay is complete.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold individual parcel rezonings in compact neighborhoods until city design rules and affordable housing incentives are finalized.
side_b_arguments: A $150,000 proffer yields roughly 3 units out of 300 (1%), falling far short of Durham's 15% at 60% AMI target within a mile of light rail stations.
Piecemeal rezoning weakens leverage to unify neighborhood design standards across the Patterson Place corridor.
disagreements.resolution: Consistency statement passed 6-1 (Charlie Reece opposed) at 02:50:33; rezoning passed 4-3 by show of hands at 02:51:44.

disagreements.issue: Townhome Density, Industrial Adjacency & Adjacent Stream Safety: 1201 Ellis Road (Item 29)
disagreements.summary: Council approved both the FLUM change and PDR 7.870 rezoning for 180 Dan Ryan Builders townhomes by narrow 4-3 show-of-hands margins (names not read aloud) after residents and members questioned density relative to neighbors, industrial buffers, and off-site stream safety along Theodore Lane.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 180-unit townhome rezoning (4 votes by show of hands; individual names not announced) given staff/Planning Commission support, modest price points (~$160s+), and Ellis/Riddle road improvements.
side_a_arguments: Developer commits to widening Ellis Road to Riddle Road, reserving 61 feet of wooded future River Road ROW along the northern industrial edge, and modern stormwater detention BMPs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose increasing density to 7.87 units/acre (3 votes by show of hands; members Bell, Cole-McFadden, and Reece voiced questions about stream barriers, buffers, and density) without stronger neighbor protections.
side_b_arguments: Higher density doubles surrounding residential intensity, borders industrial zoning relying only on an unbuilt road ROW as buffer, lacks a TIA despite Riddle/Ellis backups, and puts more children near an unfenced neighbor branch on Theodore Lane.
disagreements.resolution: Plan amendment passed 4-3 at 03:14:44; consistency statement passed 7-0 at 03:15:10; rezoning passed 4-3 at 03:15:59.

disagreements.issue: Greenfield Commercial Rezoning & Mixed-Use Integrity: North River Village / Publix (Item 27)
disagreements.summary: Following hours of testimony from hundreds of supporters and opponents, council rejected the 29.8-acre Publix-anchored mixed-use rezoning at Guess and Latta Roads by a 1-6 margin.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose rezoning low-density residential greenfields for a suburban shopping center.
side_a_arguments: Separating houses and a 50k-90k sq ft shopping strip with a connector path misuses mixed-use zoning, clashes with the Low-Density Residential FLUM, and lacks a binding site plan.
Requiring new retail to redevelop underutilized North Durham shopping centers is preferable to paving greenfields outside public transit corridors.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the proposal to capture immediate grocery investment and economic momentum in northern Durham.
side_b_arguments: Rejecting Publix misses a strong regional retail anchor and economic opportunity long sought by northern Durham residents.
disagreements.resolution: Both consistency statement (05:46:40) and rezoning (05:47:20) failed 1-6.
