meetings.title: Durham City Council May 15, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Celebrating former Durham mayors with St. Joseph's and Watts Street Boy Scouts, the council proclaimed Robert Wense Grabarek's 98th birthday and National Gun Violence Awareness Day before unanimously passing all formal votes (7-0), including the consent agenda (with Item 14 Fayette Place purchase and Item 17 Heritage Park/GoDurham ADA items pulled for brief discussion), two West Club Boulevard historic landmark ordinances, and annexation/rezoning for 815 East Geer Street. No split votes occurred on May 15, though Council held extended debate on Item 30—a proposed resolution rescinding six previously ordered 2007-era county utility extension petitions whose estimated city/petitioner costs had surged by roughly $1.7M-$2.15M due to NCDOT shoring rules and elapsed time—voting unanimously to keep the hearing open until June 19 while seeking NCDOT relief and NC Utilities Commission input on the failing Grand Oaks/Red Coach package sewer plant.

agenda_items.title: Former Mayors Reunion, Robert Wense Grabarek Day, and National Gun Violence Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis led a salute to former living Durham mayors (including Sylvia Kerchoff, Nick Tennyson, and Bill/Mary Ann Bell guests) and read a proclamation declaring May 21, 2017 as Robert Wense Grabarek Day honoring the former mayor's 1963 civil rights interim committee leadership at age 98. Mayor Bell also proclaimed June 2, 2017 as National Gun Violence Awareness Day ('Wear Orange').

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 14, 17, and General Business Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 14 (Fayette Place) and Item 17 (police/fleet/GoDurham or Heritage Park items) for citizen/council discussion and approved the remainder of the consent agenda unanimously.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017-2018 Budget Presentation (Manager Tom Bonfield) & Pulled Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented his proposed FY 2017-2018 budget featuring a 4% average merit pay pool (5% public safety), a $15/hr minimum city wage, 12 weeks paid parental leave, and an initial plan toward doubling the dedicated housing fund. Council also unanimously cleared the pulled consent items after questions on GoDurham/Heritage Park contract terms and Fayette Place financing.

agenda_items.title: Local Historic Landmark Designation (1058 W. Club Blvd) & Annexation/Rezoning (815 E. Geer St)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously designated 1058 West Club Boulevard as a local historic landmark following a brief property-tax/preservation question from Charlie Reece, and unanimously approved voluntary annexation, utility extension, consistency statement, and residential rezoning for 815 East Geer Street in sequential unanimous votes concluding at 01:43:08.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Rescission of Six Previously Ordered Petitioned Utility Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Engineering Manager Robert Joyner outlined steep cost increases (~$1.74M-$2.15M+) caused by new NCDOT asphalt reconstruction and steel shoring mandates on six county utility extensions ordered in 2007-2010 (including failing septic systems and the Grand Oaks/Red Coach package treatment plant). After affected county homeowners urged the city not to rescind 10-year promises and Council Members Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Charlie Reece debated city-taxpayer equity vs. moral obligations, council continued the public hearing to June 19.

votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous at 00:45:38.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved routine consent items excluding pulled Items 14 and 17.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Items (Fayette Place / Housing / Transit Items)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice approval at 01:14:23.
votes.discussion_detail: Clears pulled consent items after manager budget presentation and staff clarifications.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote across two actions at 01:34:29 and 01:35:55.
votes.discussion_detail: Designates 1058 W. Club Blvd as local historic landmark.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — 815 East Geer Street
votes.notes: Unanimous voice approvals at 01:37:08 and 01:43:08.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves annexation and residential rezoning on East Geer Street.

votes.item_title: Item 30: Continue Public Hearing on Rescission of Six Utility Petitions to June 19
votes.notes: Continuance passed unanimously at 02:45:01; adjournment followed at 02:47:13.
votes.discussion_detail: Continues Item 30 to allow work-session analysis of NCDOT costs, unit counts, and package-plant legal posture.

disagreements.issue: City Obligation vs. County Cost Subsidy on Six Petitioned Utility Extensions (Item 30)
disagreements.summary: Although council voted unanimously to continue the hearing to June 19 for additional data, members differed over whether Durham city taxpayers should absorb ~$2 million in NCDOT-driven utility cost overruns for non-city subdivisions ordered in 2007.
disagreements.side_a_position: Avoid rescinding 2007 city commitments made to homeowners who have waited ten years on failing septic/well or package-sewer systems.
side_a_arguments: Petitioners voted on city assessments a decade ago and planned their lives around promised utility extensions; sudden rescission penalizes them for state DOT changes and municipal delays.
disagreements.side_b_position: Verify county responsibility, package-plant owner obligations, and per-homeowner subsidy figures before spending up to $2 million in city utility/general funds outside city limits.
side_b_arguments: Other failed-subdivision homeowners in the county do not automatically pay city taxes unless annexed, and state utility/transportation agencies share responsibility for Grand Oaks and NCDOT shoring costs.
disagreements.resolution: Continued unanimously (7-0) at 02:45:01 for work-session analysis and June 19 continuation.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 1, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: On International Workers' Day, public speakers addressed unpaid jail labor before the council honored the MEAC champion NCCU men's basketball team and Coach LeVelle Moton and heard Durham County/DPD leadership. All formal votes passed unanimously (7-0), including the consent agenda—which funded purchase of the vacant Fayette Place site despite sharp criticism from Council Members Charlie Reece and Steve Schewel over last-minute process and lack of a costed redevelopment plan—an NC 55 sidewalk reimbursement agreement (7-0), and the consolidated annexation and rezoning of 3130 Hursey Street for up to 179 townhomes (7-0). Following the votes, Police Chief C.J. Davis delivered the First Quarter 2017 Crime Report, sparking substantial policy questioning from Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Eddie Davis regarding written consent-search forms, police checkpoints, and rising gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Jail Labor & Proclamation for NCCU Men's Basketball Championship
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following opening prayer and public testimony from an advocate reading a letter by a formerly incarcerated worker regarding unpaid kitchen/janitorial labor at the Durham County Jail, Mayor Bell and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden presented a proclamation honoring NCCU Coach LeVelle Moton and the men's basketball team for winning the 2017 MEAC Championship and reaching the NCAA Tournament.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Including Fayette Place Property Acquisition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda 7-0, including an agreement to acquire the former Fayette Place public housing site. Immediately following the consent vote, Charlie Reece and Steve Schewel criticized adding the acquisition to consent without a prior work-session vetting, development budget, or master-plan clarity, while Eddie Davis and Mayor Bell argued securing the land in public hands preserved affordable housing flexibility.

agenda_items.title: Utility/Sidewalk Reimbursement Agreement Along NC 55
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation and public works staff presented a reimbursement agreement coordinating sidewalk improvements along NC Highway 55 to avoid duplicating construction costs. Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning: 3130 Hursey Street (179 Townhomes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a voluntary annexation and zoning map change for 3130 Hursey Street allowing up to 179 townhomes with connectivity and road improvements reviewed against prior neighbor access concerns. Council approved the annexation, consistency statement, and rezoning unanimously across sequential votes.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department First Quarter 2017 Crime Report (Chief C.J. Davis)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported first-quarter Part I crime trends, highlighting shootings, homicides, robbery enforcement, and self-defense UCR classifications. Council Members Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece challenged the decline in written consent-search documentation since adopting written forms and questioned traffic-checkpoint practices, while Eddie Davis raised neighborhood gun-violence prevention.

votes.item_title: Item 18: NC Highway 55 Sidewalk Reimbursement Agreement
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote at 00:52:11.
votes.discussion_detail: Coordinates sidewalk construction funding along NC 55.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — 3130 Hursey Street
votes.notes: Two sequential unanimous voice votes at 01:21:23 and 01:21:30.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves residential annexation and zoning for 3130 Hursey Street.

disagreements.issue: Process & Financial Clarity Around Fayette Place Purchase (Consent Item)
disagreements.summary: Although council voted 7-0 on the consent agenda approving the Fayette Place purchase, members sharply disagreed on placing a multimillion-dollar land purchase directly onto consent without work-session vetting or redevelopment cost estimates.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support buying Fayette Place immediately to bring the land under public control for future affordable housing.
side_a_arguments: Securing the parcel before private developers acquire it preserves long-term affordable housing leverage near downtown.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support the goal of acquiring Fayette Place but object to bypassing work-session review and lacking clear master-plan and subsidy numbers before voting.
side_b_arguments: Placing major acquisitions directly on consent deprives residents and council of public vetting on full lifecycle costs and opportunity costs.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 7-0 on the consent agenda at 00:43:16; remarks entered for future process accountability.

disagreements.issue: DPD Written Consent-Search Policy, Probable Cause & Checkpoints (Q1 Crime Report)
disagreements.summary: During the non-voting Q1 crime briefing, council members questioned Chief C.J. Davis over enforcement disparities, declining documented consent searches alongside persistent warrantless searches, and checkpoint deployment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Scrutinize whether police officers are shifting from written consent searches to undocumented probable-cause searches and whether checkpoints strain community trust.
side_a_arguments: Following council's written consent-search mandate, overall search transparency must not evaporate into discretionary stop-and-search exceptions or unmonitored neighborhood checkpoints.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend officer adherence to written consent forms while preserving tactical flexibility for traffic enforcement and hot-spot crime abatement.
side_b_arguments: Checkpoints and targeted operations respond to specific neighborhood safety requests and violent crime patterns while following departmental general orders.
disagreements.resolution: Informational report concluded without a formal vote.

disagreements.issue: Historic Farmhouse Preservation vs. Prior Zoning Vesting: Fendol Farms (Item 14)
disagreements.summary: Following testimony from local preservationists seeking to save an 1849 farmhouse on the Fendol Farms tract, Council Member Steve Schewel explored a 30-day deferral while colleagues noted statutory and vested-rights limits before voting unanimously 7-0.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore a 30-day deferral to encourage the developer and preservationists to negotiate saving or relocating the 1849 farmhouse.
side_a_arguments: A brief pause might prompt creative private preservation solutions before demolition proceeds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed to a vote because prior approved development entitlements left council with only an up-or-down zoning choice without legal authority to compel preservation.
side_b_arguments: Years had passed since initial approval and state law forbids conditioning rezonings on historic preservation beyond voluntary proffers.
disagreements.resolution: Council opted against deferring and passed Item 14 unanimously 7-0 at 01:30:16.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Mar 20, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council celebrated the 43rd Annual Durham CROP Hunger Walk (now second largest in the nation), proclaimed Pauli Murray Family Home National Historic Landmark Day, and congratulated Morehead Montessori's chess team before approving every legislative item 7-0. agenda_items.title: Durham CROP Hunger Walk, Pauli Murray National Historic Landmark Day & Youth Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden read a proclamation honoring the 43rd annual Durham CROP Hunger Walk, ranked second largest nationwide. Steve Schewel presented a proclamation declaring April 1, 2017 Pauli Murray Family Home National Historic Landmark Day, and Charlie Reece congratulated Morehead Montessori's chess team and Council Member Jillian Johnson's son Elias on placing at the state championships.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (7-0) and Recreation Advisory Commission Ballot Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda unanimously (including Items 1-14 and 20-22 after pulling AT&T items 16, 18, and 19 to general business) and received clerk ballot results appointing David Folloroff with 4 votes to the Recreation Advisory Commission.

agenda_items.title: Teleport Communications / AT&T Corp. / BellSouth Telecom Right-of-Way License Renewals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams and AT&T representative Robert Darrow addressed council frustration over utility hits, sidewalk damage, and roughly 44+ inspection/stop-work interventions during AT&T's fiber rollout. Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt criticized North Carolina legislation stripping municipal right-of-way user fees while leaving city inspectors uncompensated; council nevertheless passed all three license agreements 7-0.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC16-00002: Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) Expiration Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented revised text clarifying that Traffic Impact Analyses expire even when tied to zoning map development plans, noting Planning Commission had voted 5-7 to deny the earlier draft. Attorney Patrick Byker (representing Bethpage and Davis Park) argued expiring TIAs unlawfully impairs vested master-plan developments; Don Moffitt proposed and council voted 7-0 to refer the revised text back to staff and the Planning Commission for full review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Referred Back to Staff & Planning Commission 7-0

agenda_items.title: Permanent Street Closing: 180 Linear Feet of Shawnee Street (SC1400020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Lindsay Smart's petition to close an unopened 180-foot segment of Shawnee Street along the abandoned Norfolk Southern rail corridor, dividing the parcel among adjacent owners while reserving a 20-foot public greenway/pedestrian easement. agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Initial Zoning: Mount Level Missionary Baptist Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a 6-acre voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial RS-10/RS-20 zoning for Mount Level Missionary Baptist Church at Denfield Street and Hebron Road to accommodate sanctuary expansion. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and developer attorney Patrick Byker presented voluntary annexations, a water utility extension, and Industrial Light zoning for three parcels totaling ~60 acres on Slater Road at Shiloh Glen Drive for office/warehouse development, projected as immediately revenue-positive. votes.notes: Two sequential 7-0 votes at 01:49:45 and 01:49:56.
votes.discussion_detail: 60-acre office/warehouse annexation and Industrial Light zoning on Slater Road.

disagreements.issue: Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) Expiration vs. Master-Plan Vesting Rights (Item 26)
disagreements.summary: Developer attorneys and Planning Commission opponents argued expiring approved TIAs after two to four years unlawfully modifies vested master-plan zonings (such as Bethpage and Davis Park), prompting Don Moffitt and fellow council members to pause and refer staff's revised UDO text back to the Planning Commission.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require updated TIAs and updated mitigation when large master-planned projects stall for many years so current traffic conditions are reflected.
side_a_arguments: Applying uniform TIA expiration rules prevents decade-old traffic assumptions from locking in outdated infrastructure commitments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Return the heavily revised staff text to the Planning Commission rather than risking unlawful alteration of committed development plans.
side_b_arguments: Planning Commission previously denied the earlier draft 5-7 on legal vesting concerns and had not reviewed staff's subsequent edits.
disagreements.resolution: Referred back to staff and Planning Commission 7-0 at 01:40:36.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 6, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Opening with Mayor Bill Bell's rebuttal letter to Senate Leader Phil Berger opposing claims about Durham in state Senate Bill 145, the council approved an excused absence, the city manager's priority referral of Farrington Road water fees (7-0), and the consent agenda (7-0) before receiving Chief C.J. Davis's 2016 Annual Crime Report (showing a 4% overall drop in Part I crime and 20-year low in burglaries alongside a 17% uptick in robberies and 42 homicides). On Item 17, council split and defeated 3-4 a staff-recommended stormwater ordinance amendment modifying Jordan Lake nutrient/buffer rules to align with state legislation (the electronic tally failed 3-4 without the clerk reading all seven individual votes aloud; Charlie Reece explicitly stated he would vote No to defend Durham's active federal permit through February 2018 rather than pre-emptively weakening Jordan Lake protections, while Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Don Moffitt favored working with DEQ on compliance). Council concluded with a public hearing on the FY 2017-2018 budget and CIP (accepted 7-0), where advocates pushed for a $15/hour living wage for city contractors and a major affordable housing bond.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's SB 145 Letter, Excused Absence, Farrington Road Referral & Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved a member's excused absences, approved City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority referral of Item 5 (Farrington Road water line fees) back to administration, and passed the consent agenda 7-0. Mayor Bell also read a letter sent to Senator Phil Berger correcting state Senate Bill 145's assertions regarding Durham's compliance with federal and state law.

agenda_items.title: 2016 Annual Crime Report Presentation (Police Chief C.J. Davis)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief C.J. Davis presented 2016 crime metrics: overall Part I crime declined 4% (burglaries fell 19% to a 20-year low, aggravated assaults fell 6%, larcenies -1%), while violent crime rose 2% driven by a 17% jump in robberies (68% with firearms) and 42 homicides. She detailed staffing (89% sworn filled / 59 vacancies), take-home patrol cars for city residents, body-worn cameras rolling out to Districts 1 and 4, and new de-escalation and simulator training.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Permit Modifications & Jordan Lake Rules Ordinance Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater and City Attorney staff presented ordinance amendments stripping Jordan Lake state nutrient/buffer language to resolve a legal conflict created after the General Assembly placed Jordan Lake rules in abeyance while seeking DEQ permit clarity. Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden supported engaging DEQ on compliant permit text, Mayor Bell pressed staff on detention-pond enforcement liens, and Charlie Reece opposed dropping protections while Durham held a valid federal permit through February 2018; the motion failed 3-4.

agenda_items.title: First Public Hearing: FY 2017-2018 Budget & FY 2018-2023 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson opened the first budget and CIP public hearing. disagreements.issue: Retaining Jordan Lake Stormwater Protections vs. State Statutory Compliance (Item 17)
disagreements.summary: Council defeated 3-4 a staff recommendation to remove Jordan Lake stormwater ordinance language and seek DEQ permit modifications after state legislation placed Jordan Lake rules in abeyance (only Charlie Reece explicitly declared a No vote on the mic during final debate before the un-read 3-4 electronic tally; Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Don Moffitt expressed support for working with DEQ).
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt staff's ordinance cleanup and engage the new DEQ administration to obtain a state-compliant NPDES permit avoiding lawsuit risk.
side_a_arguments: Leaving local ordinances in conflict with state law exposes the city to developer litigation and noncompliance penalties.
Engaging new DEQ leadership gives the city another opportunity to return revised ordinance protections later.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject weakening local stormwater protections immediately while Durham operates under a valid federal permit extending into February 2018.
side_b_arguments: Durham remains shielded by a valid federal permit through early 2018, and wiping out Jordan Lake standards prematurely concedes too much without guaranteed developer lawsuit success.
disagreements.resolution: Staff recommendation failed 3-4 at 01:41:19 (remaining individual electronic votes were not read aloud by the clerk).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Feb 20, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Reverend Dr. Tammy Rodman of Ash Street and proclaimed National Collegiate Transition Month for Durham Alumnae Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, while Charlie Reece announced DPAC's upcoming 2018-2019 run of Hamilton. All legislative items passed unanimously (7-0), including the consent agenda (7-0), a 1,505-foot paper-street closing at Nevada Avenue/Chester Springs Road/Hickman Avenue (7-0), and the voluntary annexation and rezoning of 11709/11711 Leesville Road (7-0). Council also approved the Creekside Commons annexation and 204-home rezoning at 4401-4413 Herndon Road (7-0) after resolving resident concerns over Creekside Elementary student crosswalk safety, and unanimously approved a 128-foot petition sidewalk gap closure on Hardwick Drive paid via HOA assessment reimbursement (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight (Rev. Dr. Tammy Rodman), Delta Sigma Theta & DPAC Hamilton

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 6, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: All seven seated members of the Durham City Council met on February 6, 2017, presenting proclamations for Teen Dating Violence Awareness and Prevention Month, Cub Scout Pack 411 Day, and Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution, and swearing in appointees to the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and Firefighters' Relief Fund Board of Trustees. Council unanimously approved the remaining consent agenda 7-0 after pulling Item 6, and then unanimously passed Item 6 (Fire and Police compensation and classification plan recommendations) 7-0 following public comment. On Item 8, after extensive public testimony both praising the East Durham Children's Initiative and raising concerns about gentrification, minority business ownership, and formal Community Benefits Agreements, Council unanimously approved 7-0 a $700,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant (requiring an exception to Resolution 9765) for Self-Help Ventures Fund's $10.2 million redevelopment along the Angier-Driver corridor. Council also held the continued public hearing on Item 9 (a proposed charter amendment to eliminate municipal primaries in favor of a general election with runoff), taking no vote while dividing in debate between Eddie Davis (favoring drafting documents for study to save over $100,000 per cycle, with Don Moffitt noting recurring council cost questions while urging no change before 2019) and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece (opposing eliminating primaries to save money or citing runoff turnout drops, voter-suppression concerns, ranked-choice voting, or true ward/council-size alternatives).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, Board Swearing-Ins, and OWASA Water Emergency Thanks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Cub Scout Pack 411 led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven council members answered roll call. Council presented proclamations for Teen Dating Violence Awareness and Prevention Month, Boy Scout and Cub Scout Pack 411 Day, and Fred Korematsu Day (introduced by Charlie Reece and accepted by Dr. Tracy Setauke/Toke of the Japan-America Society of North Carolina), swore in Rodger Lee and Robert D. Teer Jr. to the RDU Airport Authority and Alicia Grant to the Firefighters' Relief Fund Board of Trustees, and heard OWASA Executive Director Ed Kerwin thank Water Management Director Don Greeley and Vicki Westbrook for supplying emergency backup drinking water to Chapel Hill and Carrboro.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Appointments, Bid Report, Juniper St. Lease, Solid Waste Annex, South Ellerbe Restoration)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda titles covering City Council minutes, a Durham City-County Environmental Affairs Board appointment, the December 2016 bid report, a lease with Albright Community Association of Durham at 1017 Juniper Street, a professional services amendment with R&D/RND Architects PA for the Solid Waste Management annex and truck wash project, and a South Ellerbe wetland and stream restoration design contract. Item 6 (Fire and Police compensation) was pulled for public speakers, and the remaining consent items were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Taken out of order first after the consent vote, Mayor Bell praised staff, police, and fire collaboration on the compensation recommendations and recognized two speakers. Jackie Wagstaff supported raises to help officers afford living in Durham, while Victoria Peterson asked about starting salaries, veteran raises, and promotional exam fairness before Council approved the plan unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Economic Incentive Agreement with Self-Help Ventures Fund ($700,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey (Office of Economic and Workforce Development) presented a $700,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant—requiring an exception to Economic Development Policy Resolution 9765—for Self-Help Ventures Fund's $10.2 million commercial renovation of five buildings (~43,000 sq ft) along Angier Avenue and South Driver Street, housing East Durham Children's Initiative, a 100-child daycare accepting subsidies, nonprofit/small-business space, and ~20 public parking spaces. Supporters highlighted EDCI's impact on ~1,300 neighborhood children, while community critics (including James Chavis, Cameron Smith, DeDreana Freeman, Victoria Peterson, and Anita Keith-Foust) warned of displacement, property tax pressure, and limited Black business ownership and urged a formal Community Benefits Agreement (CBA). Council Members Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, Charlie Reece, and Mayor Bill Bell backed nonprofit control of the corridor while pressing Self-Help on CBA execution, local hiring, and small-business outreach before approving the grant 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Proposed City Charter Amendment on Municipal Election Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker reiterated that the continued public hearing on switching from a primary-and-general municipal election to a single general election with runoff was solely for public comment, with no vote scheduled unless Council later directed staff to return an item. Six speakers opposed eliminating primaries—warning of reduced minority participation, costly citywide runoffs, and incumbency protection—while urging true single-member ward elections and expanding Council from seven to nine seats. In council discussion, Eddie Davis favored advancing documents to study the single-election model to save over $100,000 per cycle, whereas Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece opposed dropping primaries for cost savings and raised turnout, ranked-choice voting, referendum, or true-ward alternatives.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-5 and 7, excluding pulled Item 6)
votes.notes: Item 6 considered separately immediately following this vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell pulled Item 6 for speakers; Council approved the remaining consent items on a single motion.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan Recommendations
votes.discussion_detail: Following comments from Jackie Wagstaff and Victoria Peterson, Council approved the fire and police compensation and classification recommendations.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Economic Incentive Agreement with Self-Help Ventures Fund ($700,000 Grant)
votes.notes: Required an exception to Economic Development Policy Resolution 9765.
votes.discussion_detail: After extensive public hearing testimony and council questioning of Self-Help representatives Dan Levine and Michael Palmer regarding Community Benefits Agreements, minority business access, and East Durham hiring, Council unanimously approved the $700,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant.

disagreements.issue: Proposed Elimination of Municipal Primaries in Favor of General Election with Runoff (Item 9)
disagreements.summary: During the continued public hearing on amending Durham's municipal election process, Council members diverged over whether to pursue eliminating the nonpartisan primary to save election costs or preserve the existing primary-and-general system while exploring alternatives such as instant-runoff voting, voter referenda, or true ward elections.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance administrative documents to study eliminating the municipal primary in favor of a single general election with a majority runoff.
side_a_arguments: Neighboring Raleigh and Chapel Hill use one general election with majority runoffs without voter suppression or disenfranchisement.
Eliminating the primary is estimated to save taxpayers over $100,000 per municipal cycle when primary leaders almost always win the general election.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose eliminating the municipal primary to save money and prioritize voter turnout, voter trust, or alternative reforms (instant-runoff voting, voter referendum, or true ward representation).
side_b_arguments: Bill Bell stated he would never alter election rules to save money; Cora Cole-McFadden described eliminating primaries as voter suppression and urged researching a true ward system and larger council.

Steve Schewel cited Raleigh runoff data (2003 Districts B and D) showing sharp turnout drops in runoffs; Jillian Johnson opposed changing the system now and advocated ranked-choice/instant-runoff voting or a referendum; Charlie Reece supported researching true ward voting and council expansion.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Don Moffitt noted that any potential changes should wait until 2019 given 2017 redistricting uncertainty, and the public hearing closed without council direction to return a charter amendment.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 17, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell absent on an excused absence, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided over the six-member Durham City Council on January 17, 2017, approving the consent agenda (Items 2-11) 6-0. On the public hearing agenda, Council unanimously approved 6-0 the zoning map change and consistency statement for 108 Celeste Circle (Item 12, Central Dermatology parking lot), unanimously designated the J.A. Whitted School building and 4.1 acres as a local historic landmark 6-0 (Item 14), and voted 6-0 to receive public comments on the FY 2017-18 Annual Action Plan (Item 15) after hearing urgent pleas from home-repair nonprofits and Durham Community Land Trustees. Council split 5-1 on Item 13 (street closing of Nevada Avenue, Chester Springs Road, and Hickman Avenue), voting to delay consideration until February 20, 2017 so the developer and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood neighbors could meet (Ayes: Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis; Nay: Don Moffitt). Finally, on Supplemental Item 17 (proposed charter amendment on municipal elections), Council heard four speakers opposing elimination of the primary and voted 6-0 to continue the public hearing to February 6, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the meeting, noting Mayor Bill Bell's excused absence, and Council Member Eddie Davis led the Pledge of Allegiance. Cole-McFadden presented the January 2017 Neighborhood Spotlight Award to James Clark of Autumn Woods/Woodcroft, Steve Schewel promoted the new DHIC-administered NeighborhoodLift $7,500 down-payment assistance program, and Don Moffitt recognized a community forum organized by Robin Cooper addressing violent crime solutions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Trustees Appointment, HOME Loan Pool, NC-98 Study, Water/Sewer, Paving, and IT Security)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield, City Attorney Patrick Baker, and the City Clerk reported no priority items. Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read Consent Items 2 through 11 covering the Firefighters' Relief Fund Board appointment, a HOME community partners loan pool with NCHFA, the NC-98 corridor study with NCDOT and Raleigh, Central Park waterline and sanitary sewer/WRF contracts, security improvements, an NC-751 sewer extension, Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates paving, and a managed network security contract.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 108 Celeste Circle (Case Z160006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Kyle Taylor presented Case Z160006 to rezone 0.46 acres from RS-20 to Planned Office and Institutional with a Development Plan (OI(D)) for a Central Dermatology surface parking lot with 100-year stormwater control, added evergreen screening, a security gate, and no driveway access onto Celeste Circle. Applicant representative Dan Jewell noted Eastwood Lake Neighborhood Association concerns were resolved, and Council Member Steve Schewel—who opposed an earlier UNC proposal—moved approval.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing of Portions of Nevada Avenue, Chester Springs Road, and Hickman Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Kyle Taylor presented a request to close 1,505 linear feet of unopened paper-street right-of-way along jurisdictional streams where B. Wallace Design & Construction planned a 14-lot by-right single-family subdivision. Five neighbors requested a delay citing limited notice, stormwater/stream impacts, neighborhood character, and lack of public park space, while applicant Jared Eadens emphasized the closure avoids stream crossings and Don Moffitt probed connectivity and existing 27-lot platting. Steve Schewel moved to delay consideration until February 20, 2017 for neighbor-developer dialogue, passing 5-1 with Moffitt opposed.

agenda_items.title: J.A. Whitted School Local Historic Landmark Designation (Case LD160001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Karla Rosenberg presented Case LD160001 (Belk Architecture) to designate both the historic J.A. Whitted School structure and 4.1 acres at 200 East Umstead Street as a local landmark, which the Historic Preservation Commission recommended 3-2 over two votes for building-only designation. Architect Andy Scholl explained preserving open lawns protects mid-century sightlines, developer Darrell Jones estimated ~$20 million in total post-renovation value (prompting Steve Schewel to note higher eventual tax revenue and tax-break impact than the 2016 $1.5M valuation), and Council unanimously approved the designation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2017-18 Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG, and HOPWA Needs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conyers opened the first of two annual public hearings on projected FY 2017-18 HUD entitlements (~$1.8M CDBG, ~$800k HOME, ~$160k ESG, ~$290k HOPWA). Ten speakers—including Durham Community Land Trustees (seeking HOME funds for 54 newly acquired East Durham rental units), Rebuilding Together, Senior PharmAssist, Wilma Dillard, Resources for Seniors, Preservation Durham, Habitat for Humanity, and Braggtown/East End residents—urged increased home-repair funding, coordinated intake, and rental preservation. Don Moffitt highlighted county tax-abatement options and maintaining existing affordable stock, and Steve Schewel requested funding estimates from the repair collaborative and follow-up on a Braggtown playground before Council voted 6-0 to receive comments.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed City Charter Amendment on Municipal Election Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker distributed an FAQ memo explaining that Council was only receiving comments on changing municipal elections from a primary-and-general format to a single general election with runoff, and no action would occur without future affirmative council direction. Four speakers—Anita Keith-Foust, Jackie Wagstaff, Chris Tiffany, and Jim Vara—opposed eliminating primaries and urged exploring instant-runoff voting or true ward elections. Council Member Jillian Johnson advocated ranked-choice voting, noted potential 2017 cost-sharing with court-ordered state elections, and requested continuing the hearing so residents at an overlapping community meeting could speak on February 6, 2017.

votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Council Member Steve Schewel after noting substantial improvements over the earlier proposal two years prior; approved rezoning from RS-20 to OI(D).

votes.item_title: Item 12: Consistency Statement — 108 Celeste Circle (Z160006)
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the comprehensive plan consistency statement for Z160006.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Delay Consideration of Street Closing (Nevada Ave, Chester Springs Rd, Hickman Ave) to February 20, 2017
votes.notes: Presiding chair announced: 'It passes five to one with Council Member Moffitt voting no.' Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Steve Schewel moved to delay consideration until February 20, 2017 to give developer B. Wallace Design & Construction and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood neighbors 30 days to meet.

votes.item_title: Item 14: J.A. Whitted School Local Historic Landmark Designation (LD160001)
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Designated both the J.A. Whitted School building and 4.1 acres of surrounding grounds at 200 East Umstead Street as a local historic landmark.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Receive Public Comments on FY 2017-18 Annual Action Plan
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Formally received public hearing testimony on CDBG, HOME, ESG, and HOPWA funding priorities.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Continue Public Hearing on Proposed City Charter Amendment (Municipal Election Process) to February 6, 2017
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Continued the municipal election charter amendment public hearing to the February 6, 2017 meeting at Council Member Jillian Johnson's request so residents attending another meeting could be heard.

disagreements.issue: Delay of Street Closing for Nevada Avenue, Chester Springs Road, and Hickman Avenue (Item 13)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-1 to delay the proposed closure of 1,505 linear feet of unopened paper streets for a 14-lot by-right subdivision until February 20, 2017, with Don Moffitt dissenting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay consideration for one month until February 20, 2017 so the developer and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood residents can meet.
side_a_arguments: Although the 14-lot subdivision is by-right and met statutory notice rules for immediate abutters, surrounding neighbors felt blindsided and wanted time to discuss stream, stormwater, and open-space concerns.
Steve Schewel noted he anticipated supporting the street closure after a 30-day window for neighbor-developer communication.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose delaying the street closing decision.
side_b_arguments: Don Moffitt questioned whether closing the right-of-way sacrificed street connectivity and a potential connection from Chester Springs Road to Ward Street.
Moffitt also confirmed with planning staff that 27 lots were already platted by right compared to 14 proposed homes, and opposed the delay motion.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to delay consideration until February 20, 2017 passed 5-1 at 00:56:03 with Don Moffitt voting No.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 3, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The seven-member Durham City Council convened on January 3, 2017, proclaiming January 2017 as Human Trafficking Awareness Month and celebrating Mayor Bill Bell's birthday before approving a City Attorney priority date correction (7-0) setting the municipal election public hearing for January 17, 2017. Council unanimously passed the consent agenda 7-0, including HOME CHDO affordable rental housing funds for Durham Community Land Trustees at 1207 Kent Street, downtown garage elevator modernization, a Wake County $7 vehicle registration tax interlocal agreement with GoTriangle, and acquisition of ~50.173 acres for a future park on North Hoover and Cheek Roads. On General Business Item 19, Council debated the $700,000 purchase price for ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for future Fire Station 18—exceeding the $600,000 appraised value of five lots—and approved the acquisition 6-1, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Eddie Davis voting Aye and Don Moffitt voting No.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Human Trafficking Awareness Month Proclamation, and Mayor's Birthday
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Council Member Eddie Davis led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Mayor Bell read a proclamation declaring January 2017 Human Trafficking Awareness Month, accepted by Charlene Reiss of Durham Crisis Response Center alongside outreach staff and Transforming Hope Ministries, followed by Council Member Davis leading Happy Birthday for Mayor Bell.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item: Municipal Election Process Public Hearing Date Correction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield and the City Clerk reported no priority items. City Attorney Patrick Baker corrected the proposed public hearing date for Consent Item 1 (Municipal Election Process) from January 16 to Tuesday, January 17, 2017, which Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (DCLT Kent St. Housing, Pay-by-Phone Parking, Garage Elevators, Wake Transit Tax, Eno Zone, Park Land, Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles including Item 1 (municipal election process), Item 3 (SunTrust Mortgage contract amendment), Item 4 (HOME CHDO funds to Durham Community Land Trustees for affordable rental housing at 1207 Kent Street), Item 5 (pay-by-phone parking), Item 6 (C.T. Wilson Construction downtown parking garage elevator modernization), Item 7 (Wake County $7 vehicle registration tax distribution interlocal with GoTriangle), Item 8 (Eno Economic Development Zone amendment with Orange County), Item 9 (November 2016 bid report), Item 10 (~50.173-acre future park acquisition at 632 N. Hoover Rd and 621 Cheek Rd), Item 11 (Duke Health FY16-17 grant), and Item 12 (Training-to-Work grant ordinance).

agenda_items.title: Proposed Acquisition of ~2.19 Acres for Future Fire Station 18 (Herndon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following City Attorney Patrick Baker's memo on potential involuntary taking, Council Member Don Moffitt apologized to the sellers for work-session phrasing and presented a valuation sheet arguing the $700,000 price exceeded the $600,000 appraised value once unbuilt lot improvements were deducted, while questioning siting near Parkwood Fire Station. General Services staff David Fleischer explained the seller planned to build homes themselves (foregoing 18-20% builder profit and incurring survey/subdivision costs), had graded and removed structures, and refused price reductions, while Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson cited call-response modeling and potential county consolidation of the Parkwood station. Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Jillian Johnson backed the staff recommendation as the only available parcel in the service epicenter, passing the purchase 6-1 with Moffitt opposed.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Correct Municipal Election Process Public Hearing Date to January 17, 2017
votes.discussion_detail: Corrected the public hearing date on Agenda Item 1 from January 16 to Tuesday, January 17, 2017.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Acquisition of ~2.19 Acres along Herndon Road for Future Fire Station 18
votes.notes: Mayor Bell announced: 'It passes six to one with Council Member Moffitt voting no.'
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $700,000 purchase contract for ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for Fire Station 18 after extended debate over the $100,000 premium above the $600,000 five-lot appraisal and coordination with Parkwood Fire Station.

disagreements.issue: Purchase Price Valuation and Siting for Fire Station 18 Land Acquisition (Item 19)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve a $700,000 contract to buy ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for Fire Station 18, with Don Moffitt dissenting over paying above the $600,000 appraised value of five improved lots.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $700,000 negotiated purchase contract as the only viable site in Fire Station 18's target response area.
side_a_arguments: General Services confirmed the seller would not negotiate below $700,000, was foregoing home-building upside and incurring re-subdivision/sewer costs, and had graded and cleared the site.

Across-the-street Herndon family land is in permanent conservation trust, leaving no alternative sites short of eminent domain, and Fire Station 18 sits at the optimal call-service epicenter with potential county consolidation of Parkwood.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the $700,000 purchase price as exceeding fair market value.
side_b_arguments: The $600,000 appraisal assumed five finished, buildable lots, whereas the seller is not delivering water, stormwater sand filters/ponds, road paving, or impact fees—creating a substantial premium above net value.
Questioned why a new city fire station is needed near the existing Parkwood station.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve the $700,000 acquisition passed 6-1 at 00:44:09 with Don Moffitt voting No.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 19, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized South Durham community volunteer Michael Wilson with the Neighborhood Spotlight Award, held a moment of silence for Dr. Deborah Saunders White's mother Irene Sanders and local football player Ty Brown, and unanimously referred a Herndon Road item to the December 22 work session while authorizing a closed session for attorney-client privilege. Council approved the consent agenda 7-0 after pulling four items for separate discussion and votes. All four pulled items subsequently passed 7-0: a letter of support for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit project, a $1 million-plus state-contract purchase of replacement Durham Police Department vehicles (over public objections calling for youth job training stipends instead), an interlocal agreement with Durham County for a 911 emergency communications facility, and an amendment to the nearly $2 million Employment and Training 2015-2017 grant project ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight Recognition (Michael Wilson) and Memorial Moments of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and the Department of Neighborhood Improvement Services presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Michael Wilson, a resident of Fitzpowell Apartments in South Durham recognized for his volunteerism with NCCU's Partnership for Healthy Durham and his church. Council also observed a moment of silence for Irene Sanders (mother of former NCCU Chancellor Dr. Deborah Saunders White) and football player Ty Brown, and heard council remarks praising the Scrap Exchange's 25th anniversary and Durham police officers exceeding service expectations.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Herndon Road Item to Administration for December 22 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented a priority item referring an item beside Herndon Road back to the administration, scheduling it for discussion at the December 22, 2016 work session.

agenda_items.title: Authorization of Closed Session for Attorney-Client Privileged Communication (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Assistant City Attorney requested a closed session pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privileged communication to be held in the second-floor City Council Committee Room. At the end of the meeting, the attorney clarified that a formal motion to enter closed session was also required before leaving the chamber.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-17, 22, 26; Excluding Pulled Items 16, 18, 21, 24 and Referred Item 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda titles including council minutes, multiple board and commission appointments, the FY 2017-2018 budget development schedule, CDBG and HOPWA agreements (Urban Ministries of Durham, Durham County DSS, and Durham Housing Authority), the Continuum of Care planning grant, Piedmont Reynolds/Southside Durham Community Land Trust loan extensions, the October 2016 bid report, pre-employment medical testing, and a Water Shortage Response Plan update. After clarifying that Item 10 was not pulled, council approved the remaining consent items excluding pulled Items 16, 18, 21, and 24 (and referred Item 20).

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project Letter of Support for Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda, the item sought a letter of support for funding the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project, with Danny Rogers of GoTriangle addressing the council. A council member emphasized remaining engaged on funding alternatives to uphold fiscal responsibility ahead of April 17, and Mayor Bell affirmed council members' right to ask questions before the letter of support was approved.

agenda_items.title: State Contract Purchase of Replacement Vehicles for Durham Police Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Victoria Peterson and Umar opposed spending over $1 million on replacement police vehicles, arguing the city had failed to fund youth job-training stipends to curb crime in East Durham and criticizing police shootings (referencing Frank Clark) and unmarked cars. Council Member Don Moffitt noted the replacements were requested by fleet maintenance based on vehicle wear and tear and moved approval.

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement Between Durham County and City of Durham for 911 Emergency Communications Facility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled for public comment on an interlocal agreement for design and construction of a joint 911 emergency communications facility, resident Victoria Peterson criticized low African American employment she observed at the new police station construction site and urged council to require reporting on how many Durham residents are hired on city-funded projects.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to City of Durham Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance (No. 14937)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson spoke on the nearly $2 million employment and training grant amendment, requesting outcome data on how many young men and women actually secured jobs after completing training. A council member commended staff's presentation and advised submitting specific questions ahead of council meetings so staff can prepare detailed figures.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Herndon Road Item to December 22 Work Session
votes.notes: Referred item back to administration for discussion at the December 22, 2016 work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority item referring the Herndon Road matter back to staff for the December 22 work session.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Accept Request for Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Initial approval of City Attorney priority request to hold closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Assistant City Attorney requested a closed session for attorney-client privileged communication under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), which passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18: State Contract Purchase of Replacement Vehicles for Durham Police Department
votes.notes: Over $1 million state contract vehicle replacement recommended by fleet maintenance.
votes.discussion_detail: Public speakers Victoria Peterson and Umar objected to spending over $1 million on police vehicles rather than youth job training stipends and raised policing concerns. Council Member Don Moffitt noted fleet maintenance requested the replacements due to wear and tear and moved approval, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Interlocal Agreement for Design and Construction of 911 Emergency Communications Facility
votes.notes: Joint City-County 911 emergency communications facility agreement.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson urged council to require reporting on Durham resident and African American hiring on city construction projects before the interlocal agreement passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Amendment to City of Durham Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance (No. 14937)
votes.notes: Nearly $2 million employment and training grant amendment.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson asked for job-placement outcome reports from prior training funds; council approved the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Formal Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Formal motion requested by City Attorney prior to council recessing upstairs into closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted 7-0 at the close of open session so council could convene in closed session in the second-floor committee room.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 5, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council opened with a memorial resolution honoring former City Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown and heard council remarks recognizing the Durham County Fraternal Order of Police's Cops and Kids shopping event. Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 14 (Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations) to the December 8 work session and unanimously approved the consent agenda covering street audits, parking contracts, water infrastructure, public safety radios, DPAC seating, and the Transformation in Ten initiative. Following a public hearing on the Ellis Road Townhouses consolidated annexation (including a $50,000 affordable housing proffer, whose vote fell within a truncated portion of the digest), council unanimously approved UDO text amendments for wireless communication facilities (TC1600001) and historic preservation procedures (TC1600004), the Triangle Church consolidated annexation, and a quasi-judicial Major Special Use Permit and Major Site Plan for a 145-foot University-College district building addition.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Former Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden presented a resolution memorializing former City Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown, praising her civic, religious, and educational leadership and presenting the resolution to her family. Council Member Charlie Reece also highlighted the Durham County Fraternal Order of Police's annual Cops and Kids shopping event for 30 local children, and Mayor Bell recognized Board of County Commissioners Vice Chair James Hill.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Item 14 (Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan) to December 8 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested that Agenda Item 14, Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations, be referred back to administration and deferred to the December 8, 2016 work session for further discussion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-16, Including Referral of Item 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda covering the boards/commissions attendance report, Workforce Development Board appointment, November 2016 Street Maintenance Performance Audit, parking meter and Republic Parking contracts, Durham-Orange Light Rail right-of-way donation, water line and facility contracts, public safety radio replacement, DPAC seating replacement, Transformation in Ten funding, and the 2016 COPS Hiring Program grant ordinance. Council Member Don Moffitt noted 11 appointees with under 60% attendance would receive letters from the clerk and thanked Durham County commissioners for co-funding a community health worker for Transformation in Ten.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Ellis Road Townhouses (Continued from November 21, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Jacob Wiggins presented a request for a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, plan amendment, and zoning map change to Planned Development Residential across four contiguous parcels totaling approximately 25.6 acres on Ellis Road. The proposal included a $50,000 payment to the City of Durham for affordable housing prior to final plan approval; the remainder of the hearing and vote fell in a truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC1600001: Technical Revisions to Wireless Communication Facilities Regulations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented TC1600001, technical amendments to Section 5.3.3 (Wireless Communication Facilities) of the Unified Development Ordinance to maintain 2015 standards and comply with state and federal law, following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. With no public speakers, council unanimously approved both the UDO text amendment ordinance and the statement of consistency.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC1600004: Historic Preservation and General Process Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC1600004, clarifying and reorganizing UDO provisions for historic preservation, certificates of appropriateness, and application review and notification procedures, which the Planning Commission had recommended 11-1. With no public comment, council passed both the ordinance and the statement of consistency 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Triangle Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented the Triangle Church utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning request, reporting that city water mains had adequate capacity and that Budget and Management Services projected the annexation to be immediately revenue positive. Following no public comment, council unanimously approved the annexation/utility extension and initial zoning requests in two 7-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing: University-College Zoning District Addition (145-Foot Major Special Use Permit and Major Site Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council conducted a quasi-judicial hearing for a Major Special Use Permit and associated Major Site Plan proposing a 145-foot building height, exceeding the 120-foot height limit in the University-College zoning district. No opponents appeared, no council conflicts were declared, and Planning staff member Jacob Wiggins recommended approval; council approved the Major Special Use Permit 7-0 and the Major Site Plan 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council November 21, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized Neighborhood Spotlight Award recipient Marvin Eli and celebrated Durham's #1 Digital City ranking from the Center for Digital Government before hearing council remarks denouncing recent hate crimes and racist graffiti and reaffirming resolutions supporting immigrant youth, LGBTQ equality, and Durham's Muslim community. Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including acquisition of county-owned property for affordable housing and four sidewalk grants (the consent vote fell within a truncated section of the transcript). At the end of the meeting, council debated a contentious rezoning proposal near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill roads that the Planning Commission had unanimously opposed. After an initial electronic voting error, a corrected vote defeated the rezoning 1-6, with Eddie Davis casting the sole Aye vote and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight Award (Marvin Eli) and #1 Digital City Award Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Marvin Eli for volunteering his electrician skills, supporting HOA maintenance, and welcoming neighbors. Council also recognized Technology Solutions staff and Budget Director Martha Johnson after the Center for Digital Government named Durham the #1 ranked Digital City in its 125,000-249,999 population category, citing the city's new website and IT governance model.

agenda_items.title: Council Statement Condemning Hate Crimes and Reaffirming Civil Rights Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following playful remarks on a city five-mile race, council members delivered a statement denouncing recent hate displays in Durham, including racist graffiti near downtown and an incident targeting a council member. The remarks reaffirmed council's 2016 unanimous resolutions calling to halt federal immigration raids on Durham youth, opposing House Bill 2, and expressing solidarity with Durham's Muslim community.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (2017 Legislative Agenda, Affordable Housing Property Acquisition, Sidewalk Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read headings for consent items including minutes, a Human Relations Commission appointment, the 2017 council meeting schedule, the 2017 legislative agenda, acquisition of county-owned property for affordable housing, a Triangle Regional Model agreement with NC State University, and four sidewalk construction grants (LaSalle Street EB-5703, Raynor/Rainell Street EB-5704, NC 54 EB-5708, and North Duke Street EB-5715). The middle of the meeting, including the consent vote, was truncated in the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads (RS-20 Alternative)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated a controversial rezoning proposal involving traffic on Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill roads, clear-cutting, mass grading, sound abatement, and construction stormwater runoff, which the Planning Commission had unanimously recommended denying. Although Don Moffitt and Mayor Bell warned that by-right RS-20 development could lack proffered stormwater controls or buffers, Moffitt, Charlie Reece, Cora Cole-McFadden, Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, and Mayor Bell opposed the rezoning—citing inadequate early community engagement and neighborhood impacts—and defeated it 1-6 on a corrected voice/hand vote, with only Eddie Davis voting Aye.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed 1-6 (Ayes: Davis; Nays: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Moffitt)

votes.item_title: Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads
votes.notes: After several council members accidentally voted Aye electronically on a motion intended for denial, Mayor Bell conducted a clear voice/hand vote, with the clerk confirming Eddie Davis as the sole Aye and the motion failing 1-6.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Don Moffitt noted state law prohibits requiring conditions beyond RS-20 ordinance minimums without a development plan and warned RS-20 could allow more rooftops or lack stormwater retention and sound walls, yet announced he would vote to deny. Council Member Charlie Reece said this rezoning had consumed more of his time than any issue since taking office in Dec. 2015, criticized the national developer for waiting until after unanimous Planning Commission denial to offer substantial revisions, and weighed Durham's housing supply pressures against holding developers to higher standards. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden said she listened to neighborhood opposition, and Mayor Bell voiced concern about stormwater runoff costs falling on the city under RS-20 before joining the 6-member majority voting No.

disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Denial of Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads
disagreements.summary: Council split 1-6 in rejecting a revised rezoning proposal that the Planning Commission had unanimously recommended denying, weighing neighborhood opposition, late developer revisions, and stormwater/grading concerns against the risk of worse by-right RS-20 development.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support the rezoning proposal
side_a_arguments: Voted in favor of the revised development-plan rezoning proposal rather than leaving the site subject to by-right RS-20 development.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning proposal
side_b_arguments: Developer failed to engage neighbors in honest dialogue before receiving a unanimous negative recommendation from the Planning Commission, creating stark last-minute revisions.
Neighborhood residents raised substantial concerns over traffic on Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill, mass grading, clear-cutting, sound abatement, and stormwater runoff.
As an attractive, growing city, Durham should hold national developers to high community standards rather than accepting inadequate initial proposals.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve the rezoning failed 1-6 on a corrected vote after an initial electronic button error.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council welcomed Cub Scouts from Pack 495 and visiting Girl Scouts and unanimously adopted a memorial resolution honoring late State Representative Paul Luebke (transcribed as Paul Lupe), proclaiming Election Day November 8, 2016 as Paul Luebke Day. agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Representative Paul Luebke (Paul Luebke Day, November 8, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel presented a resolution honoring Representative Paul Luebke (transcribed as Paul Lupe), who passed away October 29, 2016 after 25 years in the NC House, highlighting his tax-fairness leadership as House Finance Committee chair, co-founding of the Durham People's Alliance, and advocacy for civil rights and public transit. agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Stormwater Audit, FY16 Carryover, Muslim Community Resolution, Big Jump Project)

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 17, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized MomsRising for thanking council's universal pre-K task force resolution, honored Forest Hills volunteer Sue Watson with a Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and deferred six public hearings (Items 15-20) to November 7 due to a Herald-Sun publication oversight. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 7 and 13, closed a public hearing on extending A&J Capital Corporation's economic development incentive deadline for 406 South Driver Street while directing the City Attorney to draft three contract clarifications by Thursday, and unanimously adopted a resolution supporting the Equal Rights Amendment (Item 7). On pulled Item 13—a Construction Manager at Risk guaranteed maximum price amendment with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex—the council split 6-1, passing with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson casting the lone Nay vote.

agenda_items.title: MomsRising Universal Pre-K Recognition, Neighborhood Spotlight (Sue Watson), and SNAP Challenge Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MomsRising steering committee member Jessica Burrows thanked council for supporting a universal pre-K task force and presented a card signed by young children, and Mayor Bell presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Sue Watson of the Forest Hills Neighborhood Association. Council Member Charlie Reece also spoke about participating with Council Member Jillian Johnson in the $4.20/day NC SNAP Challenge and donating food savings to the Durham CROP Hunger Walk.

agenda_items.title: Deferral of Public Hearings (Items 15-20) to November 7, 2016 Due to Herald-Sun Publication Oversight
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager apologized for a second deferral of six public hearings (Items 15-20) caused by a Herald-Sun newspaper publication oversight and reported the issue was resolved so hearings could proceed on November 7, 2016.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 7 and 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved board appointments (Carolina Theatre, Convention & Visitors Bureau, Bike/Ped Commission, Historic Preservation Commission), the June/August 2016 Inventory Performance Audit, DCHC MPO database support, an emergency action plan contract for a critical 48-inch sewer main, a city auction resolution, and the August 2016 bid report, while pulling Item 7 and Item 13.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with A&J Capital Corporation (406 S. Driver Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey of Economic and Workforce Development presented a request to extend A&J Capital Corporation's completion deadline to December 31, 2017 for its $107,000 grant ($395,000 capital investment) to redevelop 406 South Driver Street into commercial bays and two second-floor apartments. Council Members Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt raised questions about incremental tax value ratios, contractor worker protections, and adding proportional incentive reductions if investment falls short, voting 7-0 to close the public hearing and have the City Attorney revise the contract by Thursday.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (closed public hearing and directed contract revisions)

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, the resolution urged Congress to lift the ERA ratification time limit and called on the NC General Assembly to ratify the Equal Rights Amendment. Speakers Sarah Delos Santos (Action NC) and Marina Groll (NC4ERA) applauded Durham as the first municipality in decades to re-engage with the ERA before council passed the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment (Balance of Trades) with LeChase Construction Services and CIP Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Jillian Johnson pulled Item 13 from the consent agenda solely to record a separate vote on the Police Headquarters Complex GMP amendment and CIP ordinance amendment without offering additional remarks. The item passed 6-1 with Johnson casting the sole Nay vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Reece, Davis, Moffitt; Nay: Johnson)

votes.discussion_detail: City Manager apologized to applicants and residents for the second deferral due to newspaper notice errors; approved 7-0.

votes.notes: Item 7 pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden; Item 13 pulled by Council Member Johnson.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved appointments, June/August 2016 inventory audit, DCHC MPO database support, 48-inch sewer main EAP, city auction authorization, and August 2016 bid report 7-0.

votes.notes: Directed City Attorney to clarify three items in the A&J Capital contract by Thursday (work session) for final action.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Steve Schewel requested explicit language reducing the incentive proportionally if investment fell short, and council debated closing the public hearing rather than continuing it so staff could return Thursday with revised contract text; passed 7-0.

votes.notes: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden for reading and public speakers.
