meetings.title: Durham City Council October 3, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council celebrated Mrs. Catherine Farrell's upcoming 104th birthday and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden's birthday, honored Hillside High School Paralympian Desmond A. Jackson, and issued proclamations for Disability Employment Awareness Month, Fire Prevention Week, National Arts and Humanities Month, and End Hunger Week. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda—including GoDurham bus purchases, roundabout and water treatment contracts, Police HQ material testing, and a revised method for setting the minimum livable wage—and approved Patriot Business Park's Comprehensive Plan tier change (7-0) and Bethpage Village Revisions 4 (7-0 across three votes). After granting Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden an excused absence for the remainder of the meeting, the remaining six council members unanimously approved (6-0) the 3223/3233 NC Highway 55 rezoning and the 2015 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report (excluding Policy 7.1.5d on Green Workplace).

agenda_items.title: Birthdays, Paralympian Desmond A. Jackson, and October Awareness Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized 103-year-old Catherine Farrell ahead of her 104th birthday alongside Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden on her birthday, and Council Member Jillian Johnson presented a proclamation honoring Hillside High School track-and-field Paralympian Desmond A. Jackson. Mayor Bell and council also issued proclamations for Disability Employment Awareness Month, Fire Prevention Week (smoke alarms), National Arts and Humanities Month (attended by Sen. Mike Woodard), and End Hunger Week / the $4.20-per-day SNAP Challenge.

agenda_items.title: Combine Public Hearings for Items 21 and 22 (Bethpage Village Revisions 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager recommended combining Items 21 and 22 (Bethpage Village Revisions 4) for a single staff presentation and public hearing while retaining separate votes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (GoDurham Buses, TIP, Water/Pipeline Contracts, Police HQ Testing, Minimum Livable Wage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved consent items including minutes, commission appointments, GoDurham bus purchase authorization, FY 2018-2027 TIP development, the Barbee/Herndon/Massey Chapel roundabout agreement, Williams Water Treatment Plant upgrades, FY 2016-17 water/sewer fee corrections, unscheduled pipeline repair contracts, cemetery improvements, Police HQ inspections/testing, and an ordinance revising the method of setting the minimum livable wage.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Patriot Business Park (A1600008, 4050 Patriot Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Laura Woods presented A1600008, a request by Michael J. Kane, PE to move 55.88 acres of a 101.57-acre industrial parcel at 4050 Patriot Drive from the RTP North Compact Neighborhood tier to the suburban tier to match the remainder of the parcel. Council Member Charlie Reece and another council member supported the request while urging Planning staff to clean up the Compact Neighborhood tier boundary comprehensively in the future.

agenda_items.title: Bethpage Village Revisions 4: Plan Amendment (A1600004) and Zoning Map Change (Z1600008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kyle Taylor of Planning presented a request to redesignate and rezone a 7.87-acre section at Page Road and Chin Page Road from Industrial to Planned Development Residential (4.733 density / low-medium density residential) without increasing total unit caps, while adding cementitious siding to approved materials. The developer highlighted completed and ongoing off-site road improvements at TW Alexander Drive, Globe Road, and Airport Road; council approved the plan amendment, rezoning, and consistency statement in three 7-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden for Remainder of Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Bethpage Village votes, a council member moved to grant Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden an excused absence for the remainder of the evening meeting.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 3223/3233 NC Highway 55 (Z1500017, Stallings Oil)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kyle Taylor presented Z1500017, a 2.35-acre rezoning at NC Highway 55 and Cornwallis Road (Planning Commission 12-0) featuring Cornwallis Road widening, a bike lane, and driveway realignment, with developer representative Ben Burkard of Stallings Oil answering questions on replacing an older gas station. After Council Member Steve Schewel inquired about a Trails Master Plan greenway along the adjacent railroad right-of-way, the six remaining council members approved the rezoning and consistency statement 6-0.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Durham Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Laura Woods presented the annual Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report reconciling city and county future land use maps, updating recreation open space designations, and proposing policy edits including Policy 7.1.5d (Green Workplace). After discussing Planning Commissioner concerns about mass grading, clear-cutting, and construction stormwater runoff, council voted 6-0 to approve the Comprehensive Plan amendments with the exception of Policy 7.1.5d.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 19, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council presented proclamations for Constitution Week/Citizenship Day and honored Burtwood Heights volunteer Brian with the Neighborhood Spotlight Award. Council unanimously approved deferring six public hearings (Southpoint Trails 2, Copley Farm, Ellis Road Commercial, 742 Avon/Avin Drive, and the 2015 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report) to October 17, 2016, heard a City Manager report on joint city-county Phase 1 Racial Equity Training, and passed the consent agenda 7-0. In the evening's lone public hearing (Item 18), council voted 7-0 to approve an economic development incentive agreement of up to $77,000 ($1,000 per job for 77 jobs over three years) to support a $6.1 million clinical services and diagnostics expansion off Roxboro Road and Ben Franklin.

agenda_items.title: Constitution Week Proclamation and Neighborhood Spotlight Award (Burtwood Heights)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a Constitution Week and Citizenship Day proclamation to DAR chapter Regent Linda Hester, and presented a Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Brian for his volunteer upkeep in the Burtwood Heights neighborhood. Council also recognized Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson and stormwater engineers Graham Summerson and Dana Hornkohl for stellar staff work.

agenda_items.title: Deferral of Six Public Hearing Items (11, 12, 14-17) to October 17, 2016
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented priority items confirming deferral to October 17, 2016 of public hearings for Southpoint Trails 2 (plan amendment and zoning map change), Copley Farm, Ellis Road Commercial, 742 Avon/Avin Drive, and the 2015 Durham Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report. The City Manager also reported that city leadership and department directors completed Phase 1 Racial Equity Training jointly with Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Recreation Commission Appointment and Water/Sewer Engineering Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved consent items including a Recreation Advisory Commission appointment, professional engineering services for lift station analysis and upgrades, a consultant project manager contract (SW-49C-RFQ), and a contract amendment for as-built drawings (SW-24).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Agreement (Up to $77,000 for 77 Jobs, Roxboro Road / Ben Franklin Area)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff presented a lump-sum incentive of up to $77,000 ($1,000 per job for 77 jobs created within three years, alongside $6.1M capital investment over five years and a $70,300 average wage) for a UK-headquartered clinical services and diagnostics firm employing 289 people in Durham. Chamber representative Ted Connor and Steve Hawkins spoke; Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden questioned benefit eligibility and second-chance hiring for the 18 high-school-degree jobs, and Council Member Steve Schewel explored Durham resident hiring pathways before council approved the agreement 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 6, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized Scripps National Spelling Bee finalist Betty Lee-Him Closs, marked Water/Day Without Water and Hispanic Heritage Month, and held a moment of silence for late Human Relations Commission member Norm Swicker. Council referred Item 16 (Fendol Farms utility extension) to Public Works, accepted Durham Rescue Mission exclusion petitions for the Golden Belt historic district, struck Item 3 (municipal election process) to the Thursday work session, and passed the remaining consent agenda and Item 14 (2016 Holiday Parade report) 7-0. In the night's defining split vote on Item 21 (Golden Belt Local Historic District Preservation Plan boundaries), council voted 4-3 to approve the consultant-recommended boundaries—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voting Aye, and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eddie Davis voting Nay—before passing a companion motion 7-0 and unanimously approving downtown parking meter fee changes (Item 7) following resident comments on Hunt Street.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations (Betty Lee-Him Closs, Water Awareness, Hispanic Heritage Month) and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Jillian Johnson presented a proclamation honoring Lucas Middle School rising eighth-grader Betty Lee-Him Closs for finishing 15th in the 2016 Scripps National Spelling Bee, and Mayor Bell recognized Water/Day Without Water and Hispanic Heritage Month (presented to Human Relations Manager James E. Davis Jr.). Council held a moment of silence for late HRC member Norm Swicker, praised joint city-county racial equity training, and heard Eddie Davis describe an upcoming law enforcement community panel.

agenda_items.title: Manager Referral of Item 16 (Fendol Farms) and Clerk Receipt of Golden Belt Exclusion Petitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 16 (Fendol Farms / formerly Doc Nichols utility extension agreement) back to Public Works at the City Manager's request. Council also voted 7-0 to accept the City Clerk's priority item noting petitions filed September 1, 2016 by Rev. Mills asking to exclude the Durham Rescue Mission from the Golden Belt Local Historic District.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 7, Referred Item 16, and Struck Item 3) and Item 14 (2016 Holiday Parade)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After pulling Item 7 (parking fees) and striking Item 3 (municipal election process, which had been continued to Thursday's work session), council approved the consent agenda 7-0—including Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit corridor plans, housing loan/mortgage items, water treatment plant contracts (Crowder Construction), the Great Loop pathway easement in Durham Central Park, and Durham Housing Authority Section 8 funding—followed by a 7-0 vote on Item 14 (2016 Durham Holiday Parade report).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Farrington Place South (7221 Farrington Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation petition, and zoning map change from Grayson Dare Homes for 5.5 non-contiguous acres at 7221 Farrington Road for single-family residential lots. The remainder of this item and Items 19-20/22-23 fell within a truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Golden Belt Local Historic District Preservation Plan and Boundary Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming during council deliberations on Item 21, consultants from MDM Historical Consultants explained how historic maps and development patterns informed the proposed eastern boundary around the Durham Rescue Mission. While Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson argued the historic district would preserve compatible neighborhood architecture without obstructing the Rescue Mission's ongoing work (noting no other property owners opposed inclusion), Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eddie Davis opposed the boundary over property-owner freedom and Rescue Mission concerns; the boundary passed 4-3 and a companion consistency motion passed 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Ayes: Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Moffitt; Nays: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis); companion motion passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Ordinance to Change Parking Fees (Downtown Parking Meters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda, the ordinance established parking meter rates downtown, drawing testimony from Hunt Street resident Doug Henderson-James supporting meters to manage congestion from the growing Center for Senior Living. Council Members Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel clarified the vote set rates rather than specific meter locations and asked Transportation staff (Thomas Leathers) to explore residential parking permit options for Hunt Street before passing the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Item 16 (Fendol Farms Utility Extension) to Public Works
votes.notes: Formerly known as Doc Nichols subdivision.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred back to Public Works at the City Manager's request.

votes.item_title: City Clerk Priority Item: Accept Golden Belt Historic District Exclusion Petitions
votes.notes: Petitions delivered Sept. 1, 2016 by Rev. Mills requesting Durham Rescue Mission exclusion from Golden Belt district.
votes.discussion_detail: Council formally accepted the clerk's priority item reporting receipt of the petitions 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 7, Referred Item 16, and Struck Item 3)
votes.notes: Item 3 (municipal election process) struck to Thursday's work session; Item 7 pulled by Mayor Bell.
votes.discussion_detail: Included DOLRT corridor plan, mortgage/housing authority items, water treatment contracts, Great Loop easement, and Section 8 funding request; passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 14: 2016 Durham Holiday Parade Report
votes.notes: General business item approved without debate.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Approve Golden Belt Local Historic District Boundary as Recommended by Consultant
votes.notes: Mayor Bell initially announced 5-2 before correcting the tally to 4-3 with Bell, Cole-McFadden, and Davis voting No.
votes.discussion_detail: Consultant Cynthia De Miranda (MDM Historical Consultants) explained how historic development patterns shaped the proposed eastern boundary. Council Member Steve Schewel moved the consultant-recommended boundary, backed by Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson, who argued it would not hinder current Rescue Mission operations and noted no other property owners objected. Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Eddie Davis voted No over property-owner freedom and Rescue Mission concerns.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consistency Statement (Golden Belt Local Historic District)
votes.notes: Companion consistency vote following the 4-3 boundary approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 7: Ordinance to Change Parking Fees (Downtown Parking Meters)
votes.notes: Established meter fee rates; DOT staff agreed to explore residential parking options on Hunt Street.
votes.discussion_detail: Hunt Street resident Doug Henderson-James spoke in support of parking meters to address Center for Senior Living spillover; Council Member Don Moffitt clarified the vote set rates rather than specific meter locations before passing 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Durham Rescue Mission and Eastern Boundary in Golden Belt Local Historic District
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 in approving the consultant-recommended boundaries for the Golden Belt Local Historic District despite petitions from the Durham Rescue Mission seeking exclusion from the eastern side of the district.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the consultant-recommended Golden Belt historic district boundaries
side_a_arguments: Boundaries follow historic maps and full mill-village development patterns identified by MDM Historical Consultants.
Historic district rules govern compatible future exterior construction and would not alter the Durham Rescue Mission's current operations.
No other property owners in the proposed district appeared at the hearing to request exclusion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the proposed eastern boundary including the Durham Rescue Mission
side_b_arguments: Property owners should retain freedom over how they use and modify their individual properties.
Concerns raised by the Durham Rescue Mission and Rev. Mills' exclusion petitions warranted opposing the full proposed boundary.
disagreements.resolution: Consultant-recommended boundary passed 4-3, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 15, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council issued proclamations for National Recovery Month and Women's Equality Day and welcomed members of the Youth Commission. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering Downtown Parking Garage design, testing, and CMAR contracts, a Duke University land lease, a HUD grant, and water/utility contracts, and heard the 2016 second-quarter crime report from newly appointed Police Chief Cerelyn Davis (truncated in the middle of the digest). In public hearings, council unanimously approved proactive East End / Eastern Connector land-use and zoning changes across seven areas—modifying staff's recommendation on a 7-0 motion by Don Moffitt to keep Area 2 as low-medium residential rather than industrial—and unanimously approved the Shannon Road Retail rezoning (Z1500036).

agenda_items.title: National Recovery Month and Women's Equality Day Proclamations and Youth Commission Welcome
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a National Recovery Month proclamation to Robert Davis and Paula Harrington of Recovery Community of Durham, highlighting addiction and mental health treatment gaps. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden presented the August 26 Women's Equality Day proclamation, and Youth Commission members introduced themselves.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Downtown Parking Garage Contracts, Duke Lease, HUD Grant, Water/Sewer Fees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 without pulling items, approving board appointments, pipe/manhole repairs, Chapter 70-15 water/sewer connection fee updates, Downtown Parking Garage design/testing/CMAR contracts (Little Diversified, Falcon Engineering, Balfour Beatty), a Duke University land lease, a HUD Partnership Initiative Grant, a USGS streamflow agreement, an Emory Woods CIP amendment, and MUNIS software support.

agenda_items.title: 2016 Second Quarter Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Newly appointed Police Chief Cerelyn 'CJ' Davis thanked Mayor Bell, City Manager Tom Bonfield, and the council for welcoming her to Durham before presenting the 2016 second-quarter crime report; the substantive presentation fell within a truncated portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Eastern Connector Future Land Use Map and Zoning Changes (Areas 1-7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented proactive land use and zoning updates across seven areas near the Eastern Connector. Following questions about net industrial land, neighborhood park/commercial parcels near Andrew Avenue, and the Planning Commission's 8-4 split on Area 2 (Carr Road), Council Members Don Moffitt and Charlie Reece argued against redesignating Area 2 to industrial without an active applicant given surrounding residential designations; council voted 7-0 to adopt Future Land Use Map changes for Areas 1 and 3-7 while keeping Area 2 as low-medium residential, then approved zoning for all seven areas (7-0) and consistency (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036, 3230 & 3232 Shannon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin of Planning presented Z1500036 (1.913 acres, Planning Commission 11-0) for developer Robert Gaunum, represented by Jared Edens of Edens Land Corp. After confirming the site plan included full frontage sidewalk and a direct pedestrian connection to Parkway Plaza requested by the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, council passed the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 1): Future Land Use Map Changes for Eastern Connector Areas 1 and 3-7 (Retaining Area 2 as Low-Medium Residential)
votes.notes: Modified staff proposal by retaining Area 2 (Carr Road) as low-medium residential rather than changing it to industrial.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Members Don Moffitt and Charlie Reece agreed with the four dissenting Planning Commissioners that Area 2 should not be changed to industrial without an active developer request, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 2): Zoning Changes for All Seven Eastern Connector Areas
votes.notes: Adopted staff's recommended zoning changes across all seven areas.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Council Member Don Moffitt and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 3): Consistency Statement for Eastern Connector Amendments
votes.notes: Consistency statement for Item 20.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Vote 1): Zoning Map Change — Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036)
votes.notes: 1.913 acres at 3230 & 3232 Shannon Road; included sidewalk and Parkway Plaza pedestrian connection on site plan.
votes.discussion_detail: Developer representative Jared Edens confirmed sidewalk and pedestrian connectivity were already included on the site plan under review; passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Vote 2): Consistency Statement — Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036)
votes.notes: Consistency statement for Z1500036.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 1, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council proclaimed August 2, 2016 as the 33rd annual National Night Out across 108 Durham neighborhoods, presented the inaugural Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and heard City Manager Tom Bonfield unveil the new 'City Hall on the Go' mobile outreach vehicle. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript covering the consent agenda vote and initial public hearings, council unanimously approved a public hearing item (7-0) and debated pulled Item 14 (Downtown Durham Inc. FY 2017 funding), where Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved to require quarterly diversity breakdowns of downtown businesses—specifically African American-owned firms—and residents. On pulled Item 27, approving the second Construction Manager at Risk guaranteed maximum price amendment with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex over public opposition prioritizing community investments and minority contracting transparency, council passed the amendment 6-1, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: 33rd Annual National Night Out Proclamation, Inaugural Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and 'City Hall on the Go' Unveiling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the National Night Out proclamation to Evan Allen ahead of August 2 events in 108 neighborhoods and presented the city's first Neighborhood Spotlight Award. City Manager Tom Bonfield also unveiled the new 'City Hall on the Go' mobile vehicle, coordinated by NIS to bring one-on-one staff services, job searching, and utility bill payments directly into neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Utility Bonds, Refuse Trucks, Fire Admin, Park Accessibility, Pulled Items 14 & 27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including board appointments, performance audits, a National League of Cities financial inclusion grant, FY 2017 Downtown Durham Inc. funding (later discussed under pulled Item 14), utility system revenue refunding bonds, automated refuse trucks, Fire Administration renovations, Downtown Parking Garage elevator modernization, park accessibility improvements, and the Police Headquarters CMAR second amendment (pulled as Item 27). The consent vote occurred inside a truncated middle portion of the transcript.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item (Downtown Security, Cochran Garage, and Downtown Durham Inc. Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after truncation, speakers addressed construction impacts, security in the Corcoran/Cochran parking garage, nighttime visibility of Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) ambassadors, and tracking African American business representation downtown via tax rolls. After council closed the public hearing, the item passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017 Agreement to Fund Economic Development Programs and Services Operated by Downtown Durham Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden pulled Item 14 and moved that DDI provide quarterly deliverables reporting diversity breakdowns of existing downtown businesses, residents, new businesses locating downtown, and businesses leaving downtown, emphasizing concerns about African American-owned businesses. Another council member requested women-owned business data as well, and Victoria Peterson urged using tax records and outreach to ensure minority businesses know how to apply for funding; the transcript transitioned to Item 27 before recording a vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR Guaranteed Maximum Price Second Amendment (LeChase Construction Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Assistant Director Gina Price presented the second GMP amendment (~$14M+ for earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, and site logistics) for the Police Headquarters Complex. Public speakers opposed spending $60 million/40% of the city budget on policing and building the headquarters instead of youth centers, affordable housing, infrastructure, and healthcare, while Victoria Peterson demanded exact African American firm participation figures (Price noted 83% M/WBE on package 1 and pending bids on package 2); Council Member Don Moffitt thanked the speakers before the item passed 6-1 with Jillian Johnson voting No.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Reece, Davis, Moffitt; Nay: Johnson)

votes.item_title: Public Hearing Item (Downtown Security and DDI Services)
votes.notes: Preceded pulled Item 14; public hearing title occurred prior to digest truncation.
votes.discussion_detail: Speakers discussed Cochran/Corcoran parking garage security, DDI ambassador nighttime visibility and demographics, and tracking downtown business ownership before council closed the hearing and voted 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP Second Amendment with LeChase Construction Services
votes.notes: Second GMP package covering earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, and site logistics.
votes.discussion_detail: Public speakers urged council not to break ground on the Police Headquarters and instead redirect funds to affordable housing, infrastructure, youth centers, and healthcare, while Victoria Peterson pressed for African American-only subcontractor breakdowns excluding materials. Council Member Don Moffitt thanked residents for engaging and searching for new ways forward before the motion passed 6-1 with Council Member Jillian Johnson voting No.

disagreements.issue: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP Second Amendment (Funding Policing Infrastructure vs. Community Investments)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve the second construction GMP package with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex, with Council Member Jillian Johnson voting Nay amid community opposition urging council to halt the project and redirect funds to social infrastructure.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP second amendment
side_a_arguments: Proceed with the second construction scope (earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, site logistics) for the approved Police Headquarters Complex.
Staff noted 83% minority/women business participation on package one and committed to providing detailed breakdowns carving out materials.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the Police Headquarters GMP amendment
side_b_arguments: Public coalition speakers argued the city already spends ~40% of its budget ($60M) on policing and urged halting construction before breaking ground to invest instead in infrastructure, youth centers, affordable housing, and healthcare.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-1 with Jillian Johnson voting Nay.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 20, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on June 20, 2016 with all seven members present, experiencing intermittent chamber microphone and voting display issues noted by City Manager Tom Bonfield. Early in the meeting, the council unanimously passed 7-0 resolutions of condolence for the Pulse nightclub massacre in Orlando, addressing violence among young African American males, and supporting Durham's local Faith ID initiative, along with adopting the FY 2016-17 non-exempt pay structure adjustment establishing a three-year path to a $15/hour minimum wage. In planning business, the council unanimously approved 7-0 the Witherspoon Rose Culture relocation on Garrett Road (A15-0023 / Z15-0037), three UDO text amendments (TC15-0002, TC15-0007, TC15-0006), four annexations/rezonings (Estates at Findle Farm, T.W. Alexander at NC 55, Crescent Drive right-of-way, and Herndon Road), and the Wilkerson Avenue street closing (SC1600004). However, after a lengthy public hearing over stormwater runoff, floodplain wetlands, and Colony Park buffering, the council defeated Pulte Homes' Cornwallis Road rezoning (Z15-0031), with Mayor Bill Bell, Steve Schewel, and Charlie Reece stating opposition on the record (exact electronic tally not verbally announced amid chamber AV issues) because the associated comprehensive plan amendment had failed on April 4. Following public debate over policing versus youth programming, the council adopted the FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan (voice/display confirmation without verbally announced tally, with Bill Bell, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voicing support) and approved remaining pulled youth workforce and police psychological services contracts 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Memorializing Resolution for Angela Van Doren Langley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read and presented a memorializing resolution (previously adopted June 9, 2016) honoring former Durham City Council member Angela 'Angie' Van Doren Langley (1961-2016) for her advocacy for children, persons with disabilities, and affordable housing. Family friend Destiny Quick spoke in tribute.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Condolence and Support Following the Pulse Massacre in Orlando, Florida
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt introduced and read Supplemental Item 55 condemning the June 12, 2016 massacre at Pulse nightclub in Orlando that killed 49 people and wounded 53. The resolution expressed grief, condemned gun violence, and affirmed Durham's support for its LGBTQ and Latinx communities.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Action to Address Violence Among Young African American Males
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read a resolution addressing elevated homicide and incarceration rates affecting 15-to-24-year-old African American males and listing city youth, gang prevention, and workforce programs. Speaker Victoria Peterson later criticized the resolution at 03:00:00 as lacking concrete stipend funding compared to police headquarters spending.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of the Faith ID of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel highlighted the Faith ID partnership between El Centro Hispano, Immaculate Conception Church, partner congregations, and the Durham Police Department to provide community-issued identification after state legislation restricted acceptance of consular IDs. Director Pilar Rocha-Goldberg was recognized in attendance.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Supplemental Items 53 and 54 & AV Notice)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield introduced Supplemental Item 53 (Cornwallis Road zoning map change Z15-0031 carried over from June 6) and Supplemental Item 54 (FY 2016-17 non-exempt pay structure adjustment). He also cautioned council that chamber microphones and the electronic voting display were experiencing intermittent malfunctions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 5, 7, 8, 21, 25, 46, and 54)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items covering commissions, FY16 budget amendments, BPAC annual report, Duke Belt Line Trail master plan, water and sewer infrastructure contracts, radio renewal, aquatic master plan, and youth workforce contracts. Items 5, 8, 21, 25, 46, and 54 were held for separate action.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 Non-Exempt Pay Structure Adjustment Recommendation ($15/Hour Path)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell noted the staff-recommended non-exempt pay structure adjustment establishing a three-year path to a $15/hour minimum wage for city employees. A council member moved the item without objection.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - 4800 Garrett Road / Witherspoon Rose Culture (A15-0023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented A15-0023 to change 4.5 acres at 4800 Garrett Road (former Yates Baptist Association site) from Office to Low Density Residential so Witherspoon Rose Culture could relocate from Watkins Road, freeing 8 acres near the proposed Patterson Place transit station. Nearby resident Margaret Cameron opposed potential traffic and noise, while proponents Dexter Smith and John Kent supported the downzoning and New Hope Creek bottomlands preservation.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - 4800 Garrett Road / Witherspoon Rose Culture (Z15-0037)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Companion rezoning Z15-0037 downzoned 4800 Garrett Road from Office Institutional to Rural Residential with committed elements for Witherspoon Rose Culture's relocation. No further opposition was raised.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Graphics and Signage (TC15-0002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC15-0002 updating graphics and signage provisions. No members of the public spoke on the item.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker advised that because the companion Comprehensive Plan amendment had been denied in a negative motion on April 4, a motion to renew was procedurally problematic and the rezoning remained inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan under the UDO. Pulte attorney Patrick Byker highlighted 3.672 units/acre (122 single-family homes), five 60% AMI affordable ownership homes, greenway easements, and a 50-foot buffer, while Colony Park attorney Jim Connor and scientist Curt Richardson opposed mass grading, floodplain stormwater wetlands, and Tanglewood stub-out issues. Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece stated they would not support the proposal due to floodplain impacts and UDO constraints, and Mayor Bell noted noncompliance with the Comprehensive Plan.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed (motion defeated; exact tally not verbally announced)

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the pulled budget item, speakers Victoria Peterson, Nimasheena Burns/FADE-aligned resident, and Cathy Briesch opposed the $65M-$71M police headquarters and funding 20 additional police officers, urging stipends and restorative justice instead, while Steve Hopkins supported the 20 officers and headquarters for neighborhood safety. Council Member Don Moffitt noted the Bull City Connector would be studied in the five-year transit plan; Charlie Reece supported the dedicated housing penny, trail acquisition, and 20 officers including a NECD liaison; and Mayor Bell defended the budget's direction.

disagreements.issue: Cornwallis Road Property Rezoning (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes)
disagreements.summary: Neighborhood opponents and experts contested Pulte Homes' 40.95-acre single-family rezoning at 2417 West Cornwallis Road over floodplain stormwater structures, tree clear-cutting, Tanglewood stub-out connectivity, and Colony Park compatibility, while council ultimately defeated the rezoning due to noncompliance with the Comprehensive Plan.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defeat Z15-0031 due to Comprehensive Plan inconsistency, floodplain disturbance, and tree/stormwater impacts
side_a_arguments: Comprehensive Plan amendment A15-0009 was rejected on April 4, making Z15-0031 inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan under the UDO
Stormwater BMP wetlands should not remove trees from the 100-year floodplain above Sandy Creek
Developers failed to satisfy Colony Park residents on mass grading, density transition, and environmental protections
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve or defer Z15-0031 for infill single-family housing, affordable ownership units, and greenway links
side_b_arguments: Project offered 3.672 units/acre (122 single-family detached homes) as a transition between Colony Park and commercial/US 15-501
Developer proffered five affordable ownership homes at 60% AMI, 50-foot buffer, turn/bike lanes, and greenway trail easements
Applicant requested deferral to evaluate relocating stormwater BMPs outside the floodplain
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve Z15-0031 was defeated at 02:27:39 (exact electronic tally not verbally announced amid chamber AV issues).

disagreements.issue: FY 2016-17 Police Expansion Spending vs. Community Youth Investments
disagreements.summary: Community speakers challenged funding 20 new police officers and a $65M-$71M police headquarters in the FY 2016-17 budget, calling instead for youth job stipends and restorative justice investments, while council members defended balanced investments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reject adding 20 police officers and expensive police headquarters construction without addressing racial disparities and youth stipends
side_a_arguments: Public speakers noted disproportionate arrests (including resist/delay/obstruct) and fatal police encounters
Requested reallocating funds toward $2,000-$3,000/month stipends, restorative justice, and neighborhood ambassadors
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt the FY 2016-17 budget including 20 police positions, police headquarters CIP, dedicated housing penny, and trail investments
side_b_arguments: New officers improve priority-one response times, case clearances, and include a NECD community liaison requested by the Poverty Reduction Initiative
Budget raised dedicated housing funding to a full penny and funded fleet, greenway land acquisition, and retention measures
disagreements.resolution: FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 CIP adopted at 02:51:26 (exact tally not verbally announced).

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 6, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At a five-and-a-half-hour meeting on June 6, 2016 with Council Member Charlie Reece excused absent all evening and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden excused at 03:50:25, the Durham City Council held public hearings on the FY 2016-17 budget and major land-use cases. Following reconsideration of a previously defeated plan amendment, the council passed the Hope Valley Commons Business Park comprehensive plan amendment (A15-0010) 5-1, with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, before approving the companion Z15-0023 rezoning 6-0. After Cole-McFadden's departure left five members seated, the council unanimously adopted Compact Neighborhood Tier policy updates (A15-0020) and boundary/FLUM updates for Erwin Road, South Square, Patterson Place, and Leigh Village 5-0 (after Moffitt's substitute motion on Leigh Village died for lack of a second), while approving the Alston Avenue Compact Neighborhood amendment (A15-0018) 4-1 with Jillian Johnson voting No and Bill Bell, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voting Aye. The council also approved the Police Headquarters CMAR demolition/GMP contract (Item 22) 4-1, with Jillian Johnson voting No and Bill Bell, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, after Johnson voiced opposition during the budget hearing and item vote; passed a $100,000 revitalization grant for 2201 Angier Avenue (Item 39) despite Johnson's concern over missing community benefits; and unanimously approved Habitable Space LLC (Item 40), a downtown parking garage design amendment (Item 13), and a restricted 549 Continental Drive sewer UEA (Item 43).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Council Member Charlie Reece
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell entertained a motion to excuse Council Member Charlie Reece from the June 6, 2016 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 22)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted on the consent agenda with Item 22 (Police Headquarters CMAR demolition/GMP contract) pulled by a public speaker for separate consideration.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change Continuance - Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the scheduled continuance request for Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes) and continued the public hearing to the June 20, 2016 City Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Code Amendments on Solid Waste, Undergrowth, Trash, and Junked Vehicles
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered Neighborhood Improvement Services / Priority Residential Improvement Program (PRIP) code amendments tightening enforcement timelines and penalties on overgrown lots, trash, and junk vehicles.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Revitalization Grant - 2201 Angier Avenue LLC ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Chris Dickey presented a $100,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant alongside $400,000 private investment (with $125,000 committed to Durham-based contractors) to renovate 2201 Angier Avenue for retail/service space. Jillian Johnson expressed discomfort voting for the grant without a tenant in place and legally binding community benefits/local hiring guarantees, while Eddie Davis, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Steve Schewel supported neighborhood commercial investment.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement - Habitable Space LLC ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD presented a $100,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant (alongside $722,000 private investment) for Wendy Woods / Habitable Space LLC to convert a former church/gas station on West Chapel Hill Street into a restaurant creating ~30-36 living-wage jobs. Jillian Johnson welcomed the applicant's local residency, living-wage practice, and neighborhood hiring commitment.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Parking Garage Design Contract Amendment & Affordable Housing Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved a design amendment for the planned Morgan Street downtown parking garage incorporating an analysis of pairing affordable housing units with the garage structure.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson opened the formal FY 2016-17 budget and CIP public hearing. Numerous residents spoke on affordable housing, tree canopy funding, GoDurham / Bull City Connector bus routes (including free fares and East Durham access), and over 15 speakers from FADE/All Of Us Or None/community groups urged council to reject funding 20 new police officers and a ~$65M-$71M police headquarters in favor of root-cause investments.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment & Rezoning - Hope Valley Commons Business Park (A15-0010 / Z15-0023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from April 4, council first voted 5-1 on a motion to reconsider/renew the previously defeated Office-to-Commercial Future Land Use Map amendment (A15-0010) to allow a self-storage facility near NC 54 and NC 751, with Don Moffitt voting No. Council then approved A15-0010 5-1 (Don Moffitt voting No), approved Z15-0023 rezoning 6-0, and adopted both consistency statements 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Compact Neighborhood Tier Policy Updates (A15-0020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Compact Neighborhood Tier policy updates (A15-0020) revising density, transit-oriented design, and affordable housing coordination around planned light-rail station areas. At 03:50:25 Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden was excused, leaving five council members present.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Erwin Road Compact Neighborhood Boundary/FLUM (A15-0017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on Compact Neighborhood Tier boundaries and Future Land Use Map designations for the Erwin Road station area (A15-0017) alongside Items 34-37.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Alston Avenue Compact Neighborhood Boundary/FLUM (A15-0018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following joint public comment across the Compact Neighborhood station area maps regarding affordable housing displacement and station boundaries along Alston Avenue, council approved A15-0018 by a 4-1 vote with Jillian Johnson dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - South Square / MLK Parkway Compact Neighborhood Boundary/FLUM (A15-0016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted on the Compact Neighborhood Tier boundary and FLUM designations for the South Square / MLK Parkway transit station area (A15-0016).

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Patterson Place Compact Neighborhood Boundary/FLUM (A15-0015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the Compact Neighborhood Tier boundary and FLUM updates for the Patterson Place transit station area (A15-0015).

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Leigh Village Compact Neighborhood Boundary/FLUM
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the Leigh Village Compact Neighborhood boundaries, Don Moffitt offered a substitute motion to exclude areas west of George King Road and south of NC 54, arguing suburban/lower-density neighborhoods should remain excluded; Steve Schewel questioned the motion and it died for lack of a second. The main motion then passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Demolition & GMP Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council acted on pulled Consent Item 22 authorizing the Police Headquarters CMAR pre-construction/demolition GMP contract after dozens of speakers during the budget hearing opposed spending ~$65M-$71M on a new headquarters.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Moffitt offered a substitute motion approving a sewer-only utility extension agreement for 549 Continental Drive conditioned on restricting further subdivision.

agenda_items.title: Memorializing Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted on Item 44, a memorializing resolution, immediately prior to adjournment.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 16, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: All seven Durham City Council members convened on May 16, 2016 to receive City Manager Tom Bonfield's FY 2016-17 proposed budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan presentation (Item 16), which council unanimously accepted 7-0 following questions on affordable housing, employee compensation, and police staffing. meetings.title: Durham City Council May 2, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present on May 2, 2016, the Durham City Council began by unanimously adopting resolutions memorializing former council member Angela Langley and supporting Black boys and young men (both 7-0) and approving the consent agenda 7-0. Under General Business Item 13, Interim Police Chief Larry Smith presented the Q1 2016 Crime Report and reflected on community policing and rising armed robberies and drug-turf gun violence ahead of his June 24/July 1 retirement. The main policy debate centered on Item 19, the proposed new downtown parking garage procurement on Morgan Street: local developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could be delivered sooner and incorporate rooftop affordable housing units, while administration staff warned rebidding to add housing could push an RFP to early 2017 and delay downtown projects. Council voted unanimously 7-0 to defer the parking garage decision two weeks to the work session so staff could detail timeline constraints, affected downtown developments, and affordable housing options.

agenda_items.title: Mental Health Proclamation, Angela Langley Memorial Resolution, and Resolution Supporting Black Boys/Young Men
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a proclamation on mental health and substance abuse recovery, council voted 7-0 to draft a memorializing resolution for former Council Member Angela Langley and voted 7-0 in general support of a resolution addressing challenges facing Black boys and young men.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles, noting Items 13 and 19 were on the General Business Agenda, and council approved the full consent agenda unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Q1 2016 Crime Report Presentation by Interim Police Chief Larry Smith
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Police Chief Larry Smith presented Q1 2016 crime statistics, noting violent gun crime confiscations (68 firearms), elevated armed robberies, declining burglaries under predictive RAPID/WRAP patrol initiatives, and recent homicides linked to street-level drug turf disputes. Council members praised Smith's leadership ahead of his June 24 / July 1 retirement as incoming Chief Cerelyn 'CJ' Davis prepared to take office.

agenda_items.title: Proposed New Downtown Parking Garage Procurement and Affordable Housing Integration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Terry Bellamy/staff (with Terry/Tony Leathers) requested approval to maintain the existing procurement timeline for a new downtown parking garage without re-scoping to include affordable housing. Developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could finish in 2017 and support 24+ affordable apartments over retail, whereas Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell warned a mixed-use RFP/legal/management re-scope could delay an RFQ until early 2017; council unanimously voted 7-0 to defer two weeks for detailed answers.

votes.item_title: Resolution Memorializing Former Council Member Angela Langley
votes.notes: Unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed preparation/adoption of a resolution honoring Angela Langley.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Proposed New Downtown Parking Garage Procurement (Two-Week Deferral)
votes.notes: Steve Schewel seconded and asked staff to detail Opportunity Cost on Liberty/Old and transit-oriented affordable housing.
votes.discussion_detail: Deferred Item 19 for two weeks to the May work session for staff to explain the 2017 RFQ timeline, downtown developments dependent on garage timing, and tradeoffs of integrating affordable housing.

disagreements.issue: Downtown Parking Garage Delivery Timeline vs. Integrating Affordable Housing
disagreements.summary: Staff and Downtown Durham stakeholders urged proceeding immediately with the standalone Morgan Street parking garage procurement, while Mayor Bell and council members questioned why affordable housing over the garage had not been fully evaluated before voting 7-0 to defer two weeks for answers.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore integrating affordable housing and faster cast-in-place delivery before locking in standalone garage design
side_a_arguments: Developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could finish in 2017 and accommodate ~24 affordable housing units above retail
Unanswered questions remained on income targeting (60% vs 80% AMI), Penny for Housing subsidy, and Durham Community Land Trust management
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against re-scoping if multi-month legal/RFP delays stall critical downtown parking and divert housing staff
side_b_arguments: Staff estimated researching ownership/rental legalities and releasing a mixed-use RFQ could push procurement to early 2017
Steve Schewel cautioned that staff work on 24 garage units could pull capacity from Liberty Street and other large affordable housing priorities
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 at 01:57:00 to defer two weeks to allow staff to present feasibility details, staffing tradeoffs, and affected downtown developments.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 4, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: On April 4, 2016, all seven Durham City Council members addressed major land-use disputes, an industrial recruitment incentive, and municipal workforce concerns. After unanimously approving Rosewalk at Club Boulevard (Z15-0020) 7-0, West Point 751 Revision 3 7-0, and the Acadia/Greston street closing 7-0, the council split 3-4 to defeat Item 19, the Hope Valley Commons Business Park comprehensive plan amendment (A15-0010), with Bill Bell, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, and Charlie Reece voting No and Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, and Eddie Davis voting Aye, before continuing companion rezoning Z15-0023 for four cycles. On Item 23, the Cornwallis Road comprehensive plan amendment for Pulte Homes, the council voted 6-1 to adopt the Planning Commission's recommendation to deny the amendment, with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, and then voted 6-1 (Don Moffitt voting No) to continue companion rezoning Z15-0031 until June 6. The council also unanimously approved 7-0 a $200,000 economic development incentive for Aurobindo Pharma USA (200 manufacturing/R&D jobs) and adopted FY 2016-17 Budget Development Guidelines 7-0 after UE150 municipal workers urged pay, promotion, and grievance reforms.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 21, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Returning from a February 15 continuance with all seven members present on March 21, 2016, the Durham City Council held decisive votes on two major transit-corridor rezonings in Southwest Durham. After intense debate pitting the council's 15% affordable housing goal and comprehensive station-area design planning against avoiding low-density by-right single-family sprawl, the council approved Wood Partners' Farrington Mixed Use rezoning (Z15-0009, 500-600 units with 20 affordable Phase 2 apartments and $1.7M in road improvements) by a narrow 4-3 vote, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting No, before passing the consistency statement 7-0. Next, on the Straw Valley mixed-use rezoning at 5441 New Hope Commons Drive (Z14-033), the council passed the project 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No and the remaining six members voting Aye, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement. The council also unanimously approved 7-0 a $95 million installment financing contract resolution, the 3708 Daniel Lane consolidated annexation (BDG1500011), and pulled Item 10 authorizing negotiation to purchase the former Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau facility.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 6 & 13 Supplemental Revisions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented supplemental HIDTA grant documentation on Item 6 (FY15-16 budget amendments) and effective-date corrections on Item 13 (equal business opportunity contracting ordinance).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items including appointments, audits, Brown Green Apartments TEFRA financing, Southside Phase II site agreement, Michie Lake management, equal business opportunity ordinance, DPAC deed extension, and Edgemont Park parcel acquisitions. Council Member Charlie Reece pulled Item 10.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing - $95 Million Installment Financing Contract Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff Chad Cowan presented a public hearing authorizing negotiation of a variable-rate line-of-credit style installment financing contract up to $95 million (at 68.5% of 1-month LIBOR + 0.37%, effective ~0.64%). Council Member Steve Schewel verified draw-down mechanics and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Wood Partners)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from February 15, Wood Partners attorney Ken Spalding and developer Deb Anderson defended Z15-0009 (19.95 acres at 5708 Farrington Road for 500-600 units, office space, $1.7M in NC 54/Farrington intersection upgrades, and 20 affordable units in Phase 2). Opponents Margaret Miller, Debbie McCarthy, Becky Winders, and Spencer Bradford argued 20 units fell far short of the 15% affordable housing goal and urged waiting for Leigh Village design district and housing incentives. Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis, and Moffitt cited transit ridership, road improvements, and avoiding RS-20 single-family sprawl, passing Z15-0009 4-3 over opposition from Johnson, Reece, and Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Straw Valley (Z14-033, 5441 New Hope Commons Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented Z14-033 rezoning 4.53 acres near I-40 and New Hope Commons Drive to Mixed Use with Development Plan for up to 50 residential units, 25,000 sq ft office, 50,000 sq ft commercial, underground courtyard parking, pedestrian ramps, bus shelter, and half-signal traffic improvements. Neighbor Jim Doer questioned traffic stacking and sidewalks, Don Moffitt questioned non-binding affordable housing remarks from Planning Commission, and council approved Z14-033 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Initial Zoning - 3708 Daniel Lane (BDG1500011 / Z16-0028)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented voluntary annexation and initial RS-20/FJB zoning for a 3.41-acre lot at 3708 Daniel Lane for one single-family home connecting to city water and sewer (projected $251 net fiscal loss). Planning Director Steve Medlin clarified a memo error, confirming RS-20 was consistent with minimum suburban-tier policy.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Charlie Reece for clarification, Water Management staff John Grilly confirmed the vote only authorized the city manager and General Services to negotiate the acquisition, with any purchase and subsequent construction contract returning to council.

disagreements.issue: Farrington Mixed Use Rezoning (Z15-0009): Station-Area Density vs. Affordable Housing & Design District Timing
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 approving Wood Partners' 500-600 unit Farrington Mixed Use development near the planned Leigh Village transit station, balancing an unprecedented private proffer of 20 affordable units and $1.7M road upgrades against calls to wait for city affordable housing tools and holistic design district zoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve Z15-0009 immediately to secure transit-supportive density, $1.7M road improvements, and 20 proffered affordable units
side_a_arguments: Rejection risks the site reverting to by-right RS-20 single-family homes with zero affordable units and zero road improvements
High density around light-rail stops supports FTA ridership criteria while city lacks legal authority under NC law to mandate inclusionary zoning
Wood Partners proffered 20 affordable units (tripling station-area affordable stock) plus $1.7M in NC 54/Farrington upgrades
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose or wait until Durham adopts affordable housing incentive tools and completes Leigh Village compact design district planning
side_b_arguments: Ten units at 60% AMI (plus 10 at 80% AMI) in Phase 2 represents a tiny fraction (~1.7%-3.3%) of 600 units against the city's 15% affordable housing goal
Consultant Karen Lado recommended lowering base density so density bonuses can leverage affordable housing
Leigh Village design district planning had not yet been completed (Planning Commission recommended denial 8-2)
disagreements.resolution: Rezoning Z15-0009 passed 4-3 at 02:12:34; companion consistency statement passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Straw Valley Mixed Use Rezoning (Z14-033)
disagreements.summary: On Z14-033 at 5441 New Hope Commons Drive, council approved the project 6-1, with Charlie Reece dissenting and Don Moffitt probing whether any affordable housing commitments were legally bound.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve Z14-033 mixed-use rezoning with traffic, transit, and underground parking improvements
side_a_arguments: Halved projected traffic compared to existing entitlements, funded half-signal improvements at Mt. Moriah/New Hope Commons, and received 9-0 Planning Commission endorsement
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against Z14-033
side_b_arguments: Maintained dissent on station-area rezonings lacking legally committed affordable housing near Patterson Place
disagreements.resolution: Z14-033 passed 6-1 (Charlie Reece voting No) at 02:31:00; consistency statement passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 7, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 7, 2016 meeting with all seven council members present, Durham City Council approved referring the police body-worn cameras contract (Item 21) back to the administration while reviewing the 2015 Annual Crime Report (Item 12) and conducting the first FY 2016-17 budget public hearing (Item 13). After a 15-minute presentation by Interim Chief Larry Smith showing an 18% rise in violent crime and 37 criminal homicides alongside a 4% drop in property crime and 25% drop in drug arrests, community speakers from FADE, All Of Us Or None, and residents criticized police consent-search workarounds, racial equity training, and Durham County Jail deaths. On Item 22, a continued public hearing revising fees for underground utility right-of-way inspections (primarily impacting Google Fiber and broadband deployments), council voted 5-2 to adopt City Manager Tom Bonfield's compromise establishing an immediate 50% cost-recovery rate for projects over one mile and a 90-day staff time-logging period for smaller jobs before July 1 rate updates; Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece voted Aye, while Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voted No in favor of higher (75%+) cost recovery. Council also unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0 (minus pulled items), Austin Lawrence Partners' downtown completion extension (Item 14, 7-0), and later adopted pulled Republic Parking (Item 19) and DPAC Oversight Committee appointment (Item 1).

agenda_items.title: Proclamations, Police Commendations, Jail Investigation Comment & Carolina Theatre Closed Session Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented proclamations for Toyama Sister Cities students, CROP Hunger Walk Day, Epilepsy Awareness, Girl Scout Week, International Women's Day, and Charles Bell 'Auto-Erasure' Day. Charlie Reece and Eddie Davis recognized DPD Squad 4C officers Cone, Trice, and Sgt. Butler; Jillian Johnson arranged for Gregory Williams to urge council involvement in investigating Durham County Jail deaths; and Mayor Bell reported closed-session direction to work with Carolina Theatre on financial stability.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Referring Item 21 Body Cameras Back & Supplemental Item 22 Info)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield referred Item 21 (police body-worn cameras contract) back to administration for continued work and distributed supplemental fee schedules for Item 22 (underground utility inspection fees).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 1, 9, and 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent titles including NC-55 widening STIP agreement, GoDurham buses, fire trucks, Google Fiber license agreement, Falls Lake nutrient monitoring, and Durham Sports Commission agreement. Item 19 was pulled for council comment, and Item 1 was pulled by speaker Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Master Agreements for Transportation and Engineering On-Call Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member confirmed prior work-session questions had been answered by staff and moved approval of the transportation and engineering on-call master agreements.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Fourth Quarter and Annual Crime Report & Community Testimony
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Police Chief Larry Smith reported overall Part 1 index crime fell 1% in 2015 (property crime down 4%, burglaries at a 9-year low) while violent crime rose 18% (37 criminal homicides, 10 domestic-related), with 48% of violent crime concentrated in 13.5% of city landmass and 29 operational officer vacancies. Council praised DPD restraint at protests and a 25% drop in drug arrests, while FADE attorney David Hall, All Of Us Or None's Heather Lee, Minister Rafeeq Sayeed, and Victoria Peterson criticized probable-cause search surges, exclusion from police chief search interviews, and gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson opened the public hearing on FY 2016-17 budget priorities. Speakers advocated funding public education on a 'scoop the poop' stormwater/nutrient ordinance, expanding Urban Forestry funding and tree-pruning rules, consulting local soccer clubs on turf/fields, paying DATA Access paratransit drivers a living wage, redirecting police building funds to youth stipends, and creating post-revaluation housing stabilization grants.

agenda_items.title: Economic & Community Development Incentive Amendment - Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Kevin Dick presented an amendment extending the project completion deadline for Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC ($65M minimum downtown City Center investment) from July 1, 2017 to July 1, 2018 at zero financial cost to the city.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Revising Fees for Underground Utility Installations in Rights-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield presented a compromise on underground utility inspection fees following talks with broadband/utility companies: keeping current fees on jobs <=5,280 linear feet while logging actual staff hours for 90 days ahead of July 1 50% cost-recovery rates, while moving immediately to 50% cost-recovery for contracted inspections over 5,280 feet plus $325 reinspection and 3x unpermitted penalties. Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voted No advocating 75%-100% cost recovery, while the five-member majority supported 50% recovery and transparent 90-day cost tracking.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell pulled Item 19 to press administration for specific maintenance and security responses regarding incidents and car break-ins in existing downtown parking garages (Corcoran Street / downtown decks) alongside planning for a new Morgan Street garage.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 1 to oppose reappointing/appointing Mary Ann Black to the DPAC Oversight Committee, citing her concurrent role at Durham Tech and advocating broader diversity across city boards; council subsequently moved and approved the appointment.

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 15, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the February 15, 2016 meeting with Mayor Bill Bell's State of the City fireside chat moderated by Bill Shore, all seven Durham City Council members addressed three industrial rezonings, the initial Farrington Mixed Use hearing, UDO omnibus updates, and police body-worn cameras. Council unanimously approved 7-0 three Triangle Business Center / NC 55 plan amendments and industrial rezonings (Items 21-26). On Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Item 27), after Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit speakers and council members debated Wood Partners' newly proffered 20 Phase 2 affordable units against the city's 15% affordable housing goal and upcoming consultant report, Charlie Reece moved to continue the hearing until March 21, passing 6-1 with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting Aye. The UDO omnibus text amendment (TC15-0001, Item 28) likewise passed 6-1, with Don Moffitt voting No over unaddressed BPAC recommendations before a 7-0 consistency statement. Finally, after an emotional hour-long debate on pulled Item 14 ($366,738 VieVu body-worn camera contract) in which FADE, ACLU, and residents demanded clear public-release, discipline, and retention protections, council voted 7-0 to delay the purchase three weeks to March 7 and form a subcommittee of Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel, and Jillian Johnson to refine policy recommendations.

agenda_items.title: 2016 State of the City Fireside Chat (Mayor Bill Bell & Bill Shore)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and moderator Bill Shore held a State of the City conversation highlighting Durham's 27-point resident satisfaction improvement, downtown innovation projects (Chesterfield, Jack Tar Hotel, 27-story tower), the dedicated housing penny, Northeast Central Durham poverty reduction task forces and kids' savings accounts, DOJ crime-reduction visits to Boston and Kansas City, HRC police reforms, and Durham-Orange light-rail EIS clearance.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 9 and 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved consent agenda items including board/commission appointments, 2015 municipal election report, HRC Water Management response, Lake Michie land acquisition, Culver Street extension, and North Parking Garage upset-bid proposal. Council Member Don Moffitt noted unreadiness on Item 9 (Republic Parking Systems, delayed) and Item 14 (body-worn cameras) was pulled for public speakers.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0009) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0022) - 1650 T.W. Alexander Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented plan amendment A15-0009 and rezoning Z15-0022 for 13.07-13.25 acres in Triangle Business Center at 1650 T.W. Alexander Drive from Office/Commercial to Light Industrial (up to 200,000 sq ft, protecting the cemetery easement and adding bike lane right-of-way). Planning Commission endorsed both 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0011) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0024) - 5515 & 5517 NC 55
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented A15-0011 and Z15-0024 rezoning 3.5 acres on NC 55 south of Sedwick Road from Commercial Neighborhood to Industrial Light with Development Plan (up to 50,000 sq ft) for a pest control operation. Planning Commission approved 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0008) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0021) - 462 Stirrup Creek Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented A15-0008 and Z15-0021 cleaning up zoning boundaries on 22.15 acres at 462 Stirrup Creek Drive and T.W. Alexander Drive to Industrial Light with Development Plan (up to 350,000 sq ft warehouse/light industrial and bike/roadway improvements). Planning Commission endorsed 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Wood Partners) Public Hearing & Continuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wood Partners presented Z15-0009 (19.95 acres at 5708 Farrington Road for 500-600 units, office space, $1.7M in road upgrades), debuting a new Text Commitment 10 offering 10 units at 60% AMI and 10 at 80% AMI for 25 years in Phase 2, alongside Woodland Acres HOA support. Six community speakers (including Christine Westfall, DeDreana Freeman, Becky Winders, Larissa Sibil, Jim Svara) praised the gesture but urged waiting for consultant Karen Lado's March 10 affordable housing report and higher Phase 1 affordability. Charlie Reece moved to continue the hearing to March 21, passing 6-1 over Don Moffitt's No vote.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Omnibus Changes 9 (TC15-0001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented UDO Omnibus Text Amendment 9 covering technical updates, removing the 25% local historic district petition minimum, updating wireless rules, and adding non-regulatory UDO intent language supporting affordable housing and socioeconomic diversity. Don Moffitt voted No because Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) requests were not incorporated.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Continuance - Underground Utility Installation Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield reported ongoing negotiations with utility companies regarding inspection cost calculations and recommended continuing the public hearing to March 7, 2016.

agenda_items.title: Body-Worn Cameras Purchase Contract ($366,738, VieVu LLC) & General Order Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Chief Anthony Marsh presented a final draft body camera General Order alongside the $366,738 VieVu purchase contract. Speakers from FADE, People's Alliance, Southern Coalition for Social Justice, and ACLU-NC (Chris Tiffany, Jesse?, Jade Brooks, David Hall, Leslie Nedick, Gregory Williams, Marcus Morrow, Susanna Birdsong) opposed buying cameras until the General Order guaranteed public access to use-of-force videos, barred retention of illegally recorded footage, addressed discipline and civil asset forfeiture funding, and shortened retention. Following detailed recommendations from Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson, council voted 7-0 to delay three weeks to March 7 and assign Reece, Schewel, and Johnson to work on policy revisions with the City Manager.

disagreements.issue: Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009) Continuance Pending Affordable Housing Strategy
disagreements.summary: Six council members voted to continue Wood Partners' Farrington Mixed Use rezoning until March 21 after the consultant's March 10 affordable housing presentation, while Don Moffitt dissented arguing a delay would not change the by-right alternative.
disagreements.side_a_position: Continue public hearing to March 21 to evaluate Wood Partners' last-minute 20-unit affordable housing proffer alongside the consultant's report
side_a_arguments: Public and advocates had no prior notice of Text Commitment 10 until the hearing night
Waiting past March 10 allows Enterprise Community consultant Karen Lado to advise whether public incentives or more units are feasible
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote immediately rather than continuing
side_b_arguments: On March 21 council will face the exact same choice between this project and RS-20 by-right development; funding gap tools would take until next year
disagreements.resolution: Motion to continue to March 21 passed 6-1 (Don Moffitt voting No).

disagreements.issue: UDO Omnibus Changes 9 (TC15-0001) & Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Recommendations
disagreements.summary: Council adopted UDO Omnibus text amendment TC15-0001 6-1, with Don Moffitt dissenting because staff did not adopt BPAC recommendations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt UDO Omnibus 9 technical, historic-district, and affordable-housing intent updates
side_a_arguments: Advances consensus UDO cleanups, lowers historic district petition threshold, and inserts affordable housing and equity intent language
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose omnibus package over omitted BPAC requests
side_b_arguments: As council liaison to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, Don Moffitt objected that BPAC's reasonable proposals were not incorporated
disagreements.resolution: TC15-0001 passed 6-1 (Don Moffitt voting No); consistency statement passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Police Body-Worn Camera Contract & Draft General Order Policy Safeguards (Item 14)
disagreements.summary: Public advocates (FADE, ACLU-NC, People's Alliance) urged council to reject the $366,738 VieVu camera contract until the DPD General Order ensured transparency and discipline, while Mayor Bell argued purchasing hardware ahead of policy finalization was practical before agreeing to a three-week committee delay.
disagreements.side_a_position: Withhold approving body camera purchase until DPD General Order strengthens transparency, retention, and accountability
side_a_arguments: Policy should require officers to announce recording, bar criminal-file retention of prohibited recordings, cut unflagged infraction retention from 180 to 90 days, explicitly reference discipline policy, allow video subjects to review footage without filing complaints, and formalize public-release oversight
Without accountability safeguards, cameras risk becoming surveillance tools funded via civil asset forfeiture
disagreements.side_b_position: Purchase hardware immediately while city manager/police refine operational General Orders
side_b_arguments: Writing general orders is an administrative/managerial function and DPD committed not to deploy cameras until policy is finalized
Purchasing hardware now allows officer training to proceed without delay
disagreements.resolution: Council unanimously voted 7-0 at 03:42:12 to defer action three weeks to March 7 and assign Reece, Schewel, and Johnson to compile General Order recommendations for the City Manager.
