meetings.title: Durham City Council February 1, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on February 1, 2016 with all seven members present for a smooth, unanimous 67-minute session. Following an opening tribute proclaiming Dr. Sharon Elliott-Bynum Day and announcements praising free fitness/recreation programming at the Holton Career and Resource Center and Earned Income Tax Credit VITA sites, council approved priority deferrals/referrals and the consent agenda 7-0. In public hearings, council unanimously approved 7-0 closing 431 linear feet of Coventry Road (SC15-06) and adopted the consolidated Historic Properties Local Review Criteria update (Item 14, 7-0) alongside six corresponding historic district preservation plan updates for Fayetteville Street, Cleveland/Holloway Streets, Downtown Durham, Morehead Hill, Trinity Heights, and Watts-Hillandale (Items 15-20, each 7-0 with 7-0 consistency statements), while addressing public questions from NCCU Chancellor Debra Saunders-White and property owner representative Norman Glenn regarding Fayetteville Street corridor code enforcement and economic hardship. Council concluded by approving pulled Item 9 supporting the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Dr. Sharon Elliott-Bynum Day Proclamation & Holton / EITC / Lakeview Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a proclamation declaring January 19, 2016 as Dr. Sharon Elliott-Bynum Day honoring the late CAARE founder. Council Member Charlie Reece praised free Holton Career and Resource Center access starting February 1, Steve Schewel promoted free Earned Income Tax Credit filing sites, and Cora Cole-McFadden thanked City Manager Bonfield for resources at Lakeview School.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 4, 8, 9, and 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield deferred Items 4 and 8 to the February 4 work session and referred Item 10 (8201 Farrington Mill Road water UEA) back to administration, while noting the Holton Center pilot program. Item 9 (Center for Documentary Studies / Full Frame) was pulled due to a speaker card, and the rest of consent passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing - 431 Linear Feet of Coventry Road (SC15-06)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented SC15-06 to close a 431-foot unimproved portion of Coventry Road south of Dover Road requested by Stacy Burkhart, who explained the corridor served as her landlocked property's driveway across Third Fork Creek and noted neighboring owner Marion Barringer agreed to the single-party transfer.

agenda_items.title: Historic Properties Local Review Criteria Consolidation and Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Lisa Miller presented the consolidated local historic review criteria distinguishing contributing vs. non-contributing structures, adding flexible contemporary new-structure standards, solar visibility criteria, and public-works granite curb preservation procedures. Steve Schewel praised the document's clarity and explored demolition-by-neglect enforcement and economic hardship for property owners along the Fayetteville Street corridor.

agenda_items.title: Fayetteville Street Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took Item 17 out of order for speakers: NCCU representative Dr. Debra Saunders-White supported the updated criteria to help revitalize the Fayetteville Street gateway to campus, while Norman Glenn questioned slow code enforcement timelines on vacant homes near 1603 Fayetteville Street. City Manager Bonfield promised to share staff's recent Fayetteville Street code enforcement report.

agenda_items.title: Cleveland Street and Holloway Street Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller noted Cleveland/Holloway updates focused on updating contributing/non-contributing classifications and referencing the consolidated review criteria ahead of an upcoming expansion study for Holloway Street.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Lisa Miller explained that because Downtown Durham's preservation plan had been updated in 2011, modifications only swapped in references to the newly adopted consolidated review criteria.

agenda_items.title: Morehead Hill Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller noted technical map/list alignment for Morehead Hill properties. Resident Blaine Butterworth praised the plan overall while urging flexibility on roof materials (e.g., tin roofs) and economic feasibility in historic corridors.

agenda_items.title: Trinity Heights Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller presented conforming revisions updating the Trinity Heights Historic Preservation Plan to reference the consolidated criteria.

agenda_items.title: Watts-Hillandale Historic Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller presented conforming revisions updating the Watts-Hillandale Historic Preservation Plan to reference the consolidated criteria.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Greg Britts noted he had only signed in to be available for questions rather than objecting to the FY 2015-16 Full Frame support contract, and council approved the contract unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 19, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the brief January 19, 2016 Durham City Council meeting with all seven seated council members present. Following roll call and announcements that the City Manager and City Attorney had no priority items, the City Clerk presented Bryant Kirkcase Sterling to be sworn in as a newly appointed member of the Citizens Advisory Committee. Council then reviewed the eight-item consent agenda covering dedicated housing fund awards to Habitat for Humanity of Durham Inc., a VC3 Inc. web database agreement amendment, a North Carolina Mountains-to-Sea Trail lease, a Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce Legacy Foundation grant project ordinance, streetscape and stormwater infrastructure contract amendments, and a telecommunications managed services contract. meetings.title: Durham City Council January 4, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the January 4, 2016 Durham City Council meeting with all seven council members attending. Council presented proclamations recognizing January 29, 2016 as George Henry White Day—featuring testimony from Vincent Spaulding of the Benjamin and Edith Spaulding Descendants Foundation—and National Mentoring Month, alongside memorial moments of silence for Dr. Elia Bynum and Lois Caraway. Acting on a City Attorney priority item after staff met earlier that day with contractor Triangle Grading and Paving regarding questions raised at a prior work session, Council voted unanimously 7-0 first to approve the City Attorney's priority item recommendation and then on Council Member Don Moffitt's motion to refer General Business Agenda Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257) back to the City Attorney's Office for legal analysis. Council also unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0, covering the FY 2016-2017 budget development schedule, Urban Ministries of Durham CDBG shelter meal funding, water and street infrastructure contracts, and board appointments, before adjourning at 7:28 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the January 4, 2016 City Council meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., welcomed attendees for the new year, led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Eddie Davis to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. agenda_items.title: Proclamation: George Henry White Day (January 29, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis read a proclamation signed by Mayor Bill Bell declaring Friday, January 29, 2016 as George Henry White Day in Durham in recognition of the 115th anniversary of Congressman White's 1901 farewell address to Congress and an upcoming commemorative banquet at Duke University featuring Congressman G.K. Butterfield. Vincent Spaulding of the Benjamin and Edith Spaulding Descendants Foundation delivered testimony on behalf of partner historical, legal, and civic organizations highlighting White's legislative legacy and civil rights advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read a National Mentoring Month proclamation highlighting the National Mentoring Partnership established in 2002 and citing youth outcomes associated with mentoring, including higher college enrollment, extracurricular participation, leadership, volunteering, and career readiness.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Memorial Moments of Silence, and Swearing-In Process Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt announced the passing of Dr. Elia Bynum and requested a moment of silence, followed by council remarks honoring Sharon Elia Bynum and local business owner Lois Caraway, who passed away on Christmas Eve. A newly elected council member thanked city staff for their onboarding and assistance since the November election, and brief remarks addressed School of Government guidance on swearing in the Mayor Pro Tempore.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item and Referral of Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257)

The City Attorney recommended referring Item 15 back to the Attorney's Office to compile meeting notes and legal analysis and offered a closed session on Thursday if needed. Council approved the City Attorney's priority recommendation 7-0 and then voted 7-0 on a formal motion by Council Member Don Moffitt to refer Item 15 back to the City Attorney's Office.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 21, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: At its final meeting of 2015, the newly constituted Durham City Council met with all seven members present, welcomed new Council Member Jillian Johnson's remarks thanking staff for her orientation, and approved all items unanimously (7-0). Council adopted the consent agenda covering budget and grant ordinance amendments, a HOPWA contract with Duke University, water and engineering contracts, Southview Park management, a Human Relations Commission ordinance amendment, and a resolution supporting universal pre-kindergarten and early literacy. On the general business agenda, Council unanimously approved closing a 732.25-linear-foot portion of Woodland Drive (SC1500005) for the proposed Rosewalk residential development and approved a consolidated annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial zoning for 4.74 acres at 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway (BDG1500012) after addressing an adjacent resident's traffic, lighting, and buffer concerns.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Ceremonial Oath Administration, and New Member Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:06 PM, led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Eddie Davis to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Following an administrative mix-up regarding a ceremonial oath of office for a city appointee, Council Member Jillian Johnson thanked city staff for helping orient her during her first two weeks in office. The City Manager and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda headings, including City Council minutes, appointments to the Appearance Commission, Open Space and Trails Commission, and Citizens Advisory Committee, FY 2015-16 budget and grant/capital project ordinance amendments, a HOPWA contract with Duke University, engineering contracts with McKim & Creed Inc. and for the High Lift Station abandonment project, Contract SR-63 Wilson Street with Jeff Wilkinson Contracting Co., management of the future Southview Park and conservation areas, an amendment to City Code Section 34-108 (Human Relations Commission Ordinance), stormwater laboratory services, and a resolution supporting universal pre-kindergarten access and early literacy strategies.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Woodland Drive (SC1500005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Department staff member Jacob Wiggins presented a request submitted by Coulter Jewell Thames to close a 732.25-linear-foot portion of Woodland Drive in connection with the proposed Rosewalk residential rezoning expected in early 2016. Staff found that the street segment had been renamed in the late 1930s, posed no service impacts, held little value to the public, and merited closure. No council members raised questions and no members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: 5200 & 5204 Wake Forest Highway / Marlow Builders (BDG1500012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation petition, and initial zoning request from Marlow Builders for two contiguous parcels totaling 4.74 acres at 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway, noting adequate utility capacity and an immediately revenue-positive fiscal impact. Adjacent property owner Mr. Brinkley raised concerns about heavy peak-hour traffic, parking lot cut-through traffic to the neighboring shopping center, lighting, and fencing/vegetative screening along his eastern boundary. Staff clarified that the existing development plan prohibits residential uses, mandates a non-reducible 50-foot buffer with 80% opacity vegetation at maturity, and enforces UDO height and zero-spillover lighting standards at site plan review, while applicant representative Jared Edens agreed to meet with Mr. Brinkley during site design.

votes.item_title: Street Closing: Woodland Drive (SC1500005)
votes.notes: Associated Rosewalk rezoning expected to come before Council in early 2016.
votes.discussion_detail: Jacob Wiggins of the Planning Department presented the application to close 732.25 linear feet of Woodland Drive for the future Rosewalk residential project, confirming no service impacts and recommending approval. No council questions or public comments were offered, and the street closing passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 5200 & 5204 Wake Forest Highway Initial Zoning (BDG1500012)
votes.notes: Required separate statutory consistency vote following initial zoning.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the consolidated annexation and initial zoning for 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway, Council voted 7-0 to adopt the required statutory consistency statement.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 7, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The December 7, 2015 organizational meeting began with certification of the November 2015 municipal election results (19,494 voters, or 10.8% turnout) and farewell tributes and appreciation plaques for retiring 12-year At-Large Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti. Mayor Bill Bell, re-elected Council Member Steve Schewel, and newly elected Council Members Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece were sworn into office, and the newly seated Council unanimously re-elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore (7-0). Council observed a moment of silence in memory of late civic leader R. Kelly Bryant, unanimously approved a nine-item consent agenda (7-0) including the FY 2015 CAFR and Q1 financial report, and received Mayor Bell's committee assignments featuring a newly created Holiday Parade Committee to plan a 2016 parade.

agenda_items.title: Certification of November 2015 Election Results and Farewell Tributes to Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Chair Bill Brian and Director Michael Perry certified the November 2015 municipal election results (19,494 votes cast, 10.8% turnout, including 3,746 early voters) and presented certificates of election to Mayor Bill Bell and At-Large Council Members Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece. Mayor Bell presented appreciation plaques to outgoing At-Large Council Members Eugene A. Brown and Diane Catotti honoring their 12 years of service from December 2003 to December 2015.

agenda_items.title: Oaths of Office and Remarks by Newly Elected and Outgoing Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel took their oaths of office. Johnson thanked her family and community supporters, Schewel thanked voters, family, city staff, and outgoing mentors Brown and Catotti, and Brown and Catotti delivered farewell addresses reflecting on Durham's 12-year turnaround while highlighting ongoing challenges around poverty, affordable housing, police-community relations, and state legislative relations.

agenda_items.title: Election of Mayor Pro Tempore and Remembrance of R. Kelly Bryant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With the newly elected members seated on the dais, Mayor Bell endorsed Cora Cole-McFadden to continue serving as Mayor Pro Tempore for another two-year term, which Council approved 7-0. Council Member Eddie Davis then honored longtime civil rights and community leader R. Kelly Bryant following his passing at age 98, and Council observed a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney, or City Clerk, Council adopted the nine-item consent agenda. Items included minutes, the October 2015 Cross Connection Control Performance Audit, water engineering contracts with Hazen and Sawyer P.C. and Kimley-Horn and Associates, the October 2015 bid report, an upset-bid property sale, the Priority Trails plan, the FY 2015 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR), and the FY 2015-16 First Quarter Financial Report.

agenda_items.title: Council Committee Assignments and Creation of Holiday Parade Committee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell distributed updated committee assignments for council members to finalize by the Thursday work session. He also announced the creation of a new Holiday Parade Committee—co-chaired by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden with Don Moffitt, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece—to plan staging, timing, and budget inclusion for a Durham holiday parade in 2016.

votes.item_title: Re-elect Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: First formal vote of the newly seated 2015-2017 City Council.
votes.discussion_detail: As the first order of business following the swearing-in of Mayor Bill Bell and Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel, Mayor Bell endorsed Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden for another two-year term as Mayor Pro Tempore. The motion passed unanimously 7-0.
